title: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes
summary: The performance of medical image segmentation depends on a large amount of annotated data, and most segmentation models experience a significant drop in performance in low-sample-size scenarios. Existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised methods rely on specific network architectures, while traditional multi-view-assisted segmentation methods require strictly paired samples, which limits their clinical applications. To address these issues, we propose DPIF, a general-purpose plug-and-play dual-path interaction framework compatible with arbitrary encoder-decoder segmentation networks, which leverages cross-view anatomical complementarity to reduce annotation reliance. DPIF first performs Sinkhorn optimal transport-based cross-view distribution alignment to establish global semantic correspondence without sample-level pairing. It then adopts conditional mutual information-guided feature decoupling to enable bidirectional knowledge transfer only within the shared semantic space, suppressing view-specific noise. Finally, persistent homology-based topological regularization encodes anatomical invariants as unsupervised priors to mitigate overfitting. Experiments were conducted using 24 baseline models on a private multicenter echocardiography dataset and two public datasets. The results show that DPIF-enhanced models outperform single-view baseline models when trained on comparable amounts of data. Notably, most dual-path variants trained on 40\% - 60\% of the data achieve performance comparable to that of single-view models trained on the full dataset. This demonstrates that DPIF provides a general-purpose and scalable solution for data-scarce multi-view medical image segmentation problems.

notes_zh.digest_en: DPIF is a plug-and-play dual-branch framework that couples two independently initialized encoder-decoder segmentation networks through three mechanisms: conditional-mutual-information feature decoupling into shared/view-specific parts, Sinkhorn optimal-transport alignment of the shared feature distributions (no sample pairing required), and persistent-homology topological consistency plus bidirectional KL distillation. Across 24 backbones on a private echocardiography set and two public datasets, dual-path variants improved DSC on average by 13.33% (long axis) and 8.97% (short axis) over single-path baselines [p. 10], and most variants trained on 40-60% of data matched full-data single-path models [p. 15]. Caveats: the ablation gains are small (0.19-2.61% DSC for individual modules) [p. 14], several tables are garbled in the supplied text, and the paper does not report the actual annotation fraction used in the main comparison.

notes_zh.full_md:
## 1. 问题与动机

医学分割高度依赖标注，而多视图协议要求每个视图单独标注，成本成倍增加 [p. 2]。作者认为现有方案不足：半监督仍需一定规模的无标注数据，弱监督受粗标签精度上限限制，少样本方法在医学域间迁移效果不确定 [p. 3]。在多视图融合方面，输入级堆叠忽略视图间空间差异，特征级拼接引入视图特有噪声，决策级融合丢弃隐层互补信息；且多数方案与特定网络结构耦合，更关键的是几乎都要求严格配对的多视图患者数据 [pp. 2-3]。DPIF 的核心思路是用跨视图解剖互补性替代扩充标注，同时保持骨干无关并容忍非配对数据 [p. 2]。

## 2. 方法

**结构。** 两个结构相同但独立初始化的分支各接收一个视图，输出分割图与软概率；交互模块插入指定的编解码层，推理时关闭，因此部署模型就是两个独立分割器 [p. 3]。

**两层解耦。** 每个分支用两个并行 1x1 卷积编码器：共享权重的编码器产生共享特征 F_c，视图独立编码器产生视图特有特征 F_p（式 1）[p. 5]。约束为 L_decouple = I(F_c;F_p|G) - λ1 I(F_c;G) - λ2 I(F_p;G)（式 2/8）：在给定标签下最小化两部分的条件互信息，最大化共享特征与标签的依赖，并抑制与任务无关的视图特有信号 [pp. 5, 7]。

**Sinkhorn 对齐。** 两分支的共享特征展平为点集 X（N_l 点）与 Y（N_s 点），配以均匀离散测度；N_l 与 N_s 可不同，这正是支持非配对的原因 [p. 5]。代价 C_ij = ||x_i - y_j||^2_2；熵正则问题 d_Sinkhorn = min_P <P,C>_F - εH(P) 由 Sinkhorn-Knopp 迭代求得传输计划 P* [p. 5]。双向映射得到互补特征 F_{cl<-s} = P* F_cs 与 F_{cs<-l} = (P*)^T F_cl [p. 6]。

**不确定性自适应权重。** 每视图不确定性 E = -(1/N) Σ [p_i log p_i + (1-p_i) log(1-p_i)]，取值 [0,1]（式 4）；权重 α_l = α0 σ((E_l - E_s)/τ)，α_s = α0 σ((E_s - E_l)/τ)（式 5），使置信度较低的分支获得更多引导 [p. 6]。

**拓扑正则。** 由概率图经下水平集滤波得到持续图 PD(·)；因精确计算不可微，采用多尺度高斯平滑得到近似持续图，L_topo = W_2(PD(P_l), PD(P_s))（式 6/9），W_2 通过耦合矩阵 γ 在离散点集上定义（式 10）[pp. 6-7]。

**总目标。** L_total = L_seg + λ_d L_decouple + λ_t L_topo + λ_k L_kd（式 7），其中 L_seg 为 Dice+BCE 按视图平均，L_kd 为两视图温度平滑 softmax 图之间的对称 KL（式 11）[p. 7]。

## 3. 贡献

作者主张：(i) 可插入任意编码器-解码器网络的通用双路径框架；(ii) 基于最优传输的跨视图对齐，实现非配对数据的分布级匹配；(iii) 条件互信息约束的两层解耦，使迁移仅发生在共享空间；(iv) 以持续同调拓扑一致性作为无监督先验抑制过拟合 [p. 2]。我的理解：各组件本身来自已有工具（Sinkhorn 最优传输、CMI 解耦、可微持续同调），新意在于将其组合为骨干无关的包装器，并以数据效率作为核心实证主张，而非某一模块的原创性。

## 4. 实验与结果

**数据。** PME：429 例、5 家中心，心尖四腔长轴与乳头肌水平短轴，收缩末与舒张末帧，每视图 858 张，标注左室心肌 [p. 8]。FLARE2023：经肝脏大小与肿瘤筛选后，每视图 581 张 2D 切片 [p. 8]。MSD：每视图 172 张，前海马 [p. 8]。患者级划分：20% 独立测试，其余 5 折交叉验证；裁剪至 512x512；仅训练折做增强 [pp. 8-9]。

**设置。** PyTorch 1.12，Adam，初始学习率 2e-4 余弦退火至 1e-5，批大小 2，100 轮，前 30 轮冻结骨干，τ=0.2，T=2.0，α=0.1，β_s=β_l=0.05，两块 RTX 4090 [p. 8]。指标：DSC、IoU、HD95、ASD，取五个最优模型在测试集上的平均 [p. 8]。

**主对比。** 24 个编码器-解码器骨干作为单路径（SP）基线，与其 DPIF 双路径（DP）变体比较。报告称所有 DP 变体均有提升；三数据集平均 DSC 提升长轴 13.33%、短轴 8.97%；海马长轴平均提升最大达 19.2%；RollingUNet 在海马长轴提升 57.57% 为最高；平均 HD95 长轴降 4.27、短轴降 2.38；少数模型（如 SCSEUNet）HD95 略有退化 [p. 10]。表 1（PME）可读：如 UNet 长轴 DSC 0.7417 -> 0.8125（+9.55%），UMNet 0.8058 -> 0.8519（+5.72%）[p. 9]。表 2-3（FLARE2023、MSD）在提供的文本中行列错乱严重，无法可靠归属逐模型数值，我不做重建 [p. 11]。

**多视图基线对比。** 五种方法（AMDANet、CoBioNet、DSM、MSMVNet、PGRNet）统一使用 UMNet 骨干与相同划分 [p. 12]。DP-UMNet 在所有视图领先：PME 长轴 0.8519 对 SP 0.8058（+5.72%），短轴 0.8495（+6.40%）；FLARE 长轴 0.9824（+5.77%），短轴 0.9503（+1.05%）；MSD 长轴 0.9124（+0.52%），短轴 0.9182（+0.11%）。多数对比方法低于 SP-UMNet，MSMVNet 与 CoBioNet 最差（如 MSMVNet 在 MSD 长轴 -30.59%）[p. 12]。需注意 MSD 短轴 DP 的 HD95 为 1.9608，相对其 SP 值 6.0197 与 ASD 显得异常，正文未讨论。

**消融（PME，UMNet）。** 基线长轴 DSC 0.8058。仅解耦 0.8082（+0.30%）；仅 Sinkhorn 0.8245（+2.32%）；仅自适应权重 0.8073（+0.19%）；仅拓扑 0.8152（+1.17%）；全模块 0.8519（+5.72%）；短轴全模块 0.8495（+6.40%）[p. 14]。正文称 Sinkhorn 带来长轴 2%、短轴 2.24%，拓扑带来长轴 1.14% 且 HD95 降约 0.39 [p. 14]；而表中仅拓扑行为 +1.17%、HD95 由 12.6179 降至 11.2587，降幅大于正文所述，存在内部不一致，值得指出。

**数据量实验。** 以 RollingUNet、UNet、UMNet 构建 20/40/60/80% 分层嵌套子集，固定测试集、5 折交叉验证 [p. 14]。20% 到 40% 区间增益最大；多数情况下 DP 模型在低于 60% 标注时达到全量 SP 精度；DP-RollingUNet 仅用 20% 即在 PME 短轴超过全量 SP；文中给出的阈值：PME 约 60%、FLARE2023 约 40%、MSD 约 60% [pp. 14-15]。图 5 曲线在文本中无法读取具体数值。

**临床盲评。** 3 名超声与 3 名放射专家，1-5 Likert，每视图 30 例，随机化盲法展示 [p. 15]。PME 短轴 3.49±0.60 对 3.07±0.67（Wilcoxon p=0.004，Cliff's δ=0.57），评分≥4 比例由 24.4% 升至 52.2%；FLARE 长轴 p=0.035；MSD 长轴 p=0.049；PME 长轴、FLARE 短轴、MSD 短轴不显著（p=0.647、0.917、0.519）[p. 15]。

## 5. 评估

有支持的结论：DPIF 在多种骨干上普遍优于自身 SP 基线，数据效率趋势在三个数据集与三个骨干上一致。不足或缺失：(a) 主对比实验的标注预算从未说明，"可比数据量"无法核实；(b) 单模块消融增益很小，且拓扑行与正文数字冲突；(c) 表 2-3 在此不可读，13.33%/8.97% 的总体均值无法核验；(d) 分割指标无统计检验，仅读者评分有检验；(e) 未报告双路径训练的计算/时延开销；(f) 非配对能力未用刻意非配对的数据验证。作者自述局限：仅支持两视图，可微持续同调近似可能遗漏细微拓扑特征 [p. 17]。

## 6. 复现

已报告：PyTorch 1.12；Adam；学习率 2e-4 至 1e-5 余弦；批大小 2；100 轮；骨干冻结 30 轮；τ=0.2；T=2.0；α=0.1；β_s=β_l=0.05；512x512；患者级 20% 测试 + 5 折交叉验证；仅训练折增强；两块 RTX 4090 [pp. 8-9]。未报告：λ_d、λ_t、λ_k 的取值（4.3 节的 α/β 符号与式 7 的 λ 无法一一对应）；Sinkhorn 的 ε 与迭代次数；高斯平滑尺度；ODI 插入的具体层；所用 CMI 估计器；主对比中标注样本数量；代码与数据可得性。这些需向作者或代码发布获取。

notes_en.full_md:
## 1. Problem and motivation

Medical segmentation is annotation-hungry, and multi-view protocols multiply the cost because each view must be labeled separately [p. 2]. The authors argue that existing remedies are insufficient: semi-supervised methods still need a sizeable unlabeled pool, weakly supervised methods have an accuracy ceiling from coarse labels, and few-shot methods transfer poorly across medical domains [p. 3]. For multi-view fusion, input-level stacking ignores inter-view spatial differences, feature-level concatenation admits view-specific noise, and decision-level fusion discards hidden-layer complementarity; most such schemes are architecture-bound and, critically, require strictly paired multi-view patient data [pp. 2-3]. DPIF's premise is to substitute cross-view anatomical complementarity for additional annotations while remaining backbone-agnostic and tolerant of unpaired data [p. 2].

## 2. Method

**Architecture.** Two branches with identical structure but independent initialization each take one view and output a segmentation map and soft probabilities; the interaction module is inserted at selected encoder-decoder layers and is disabled at inference, so the deployed model is just two independent segmenters [p. 3].

**Two-layer decoupling.** Each branch uses two parallel 1x1 conv encoders: a weight-shared encoder producing shared features F_c and a view-independent encoder producing view-specific F_p (Eq. 1) [p. 5]. The constraint is L_decouple = I(F_c;F_p|G) - λ1 I(F_c;G) - λ2 I(F_p;G) (Eq. 2/8): minimize conditional mutual information between the two parts given labels, maximize shared-feature/label dependence, and suppress task-irrelevant view-specific signal [pp. 5, 7].

**Sinkhorn alignment.** Shared features from each branch are flattened into point sets X (N_l points) and Y (N_s points) with uniform discrete measures; N_l and N_s may differ, which is what permits unpaired use [p. 5]. Cost C_ij = ||x_i - y_j||^2_2; the entropy-regularized problem d_Sinkhorn = min_P <P,C>_F - εH(P) is solved by Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations to give plan P* [p. 5]. Bidirectional mapping then yields complementary features F_{cl<-s} = P* F_cs and F_{cs<-l} = (P*)^T F_cl [p. 6].

**Uncertainty-adaptive weights.** Per-view uncertainty E = -(1/N) Σ [p_i log p_i + (1-p_i) log(1-p_i)] in [0,1] (Eq. 4); weights α_l = α0 σ((E_l - E_s)/τ), α_s = α0 σ((E_s - E_l)/τ) (Eq. 5), so the less confident branch receives more guidance [p. 6].

**Topological regularization.** Persistence diagrams PD(·) are extracted from probability maps by sublevel-set filtration; because exact computation is non-differentiable, multiscale Gaussian smoothing gives an approximate diagram, and L_topo = W_2(PD(P_l), PD(P_s)) (Eq. 6/9), with W_2 defined over discrete point sets via a coupling matrix γ (Eq. 10) [pp. 6-7].

**Total objective.** L_total = L_seg + λ_d L_decouple + λ_t L_topo + λ_k L_kd (Eq. 7), where L_seg is Dice+BCE averaged per view and L_kd is symmetric KL between temperature-smoothed softmax maps of the two views (Eq. 11) [p. 7].

## 3. Contribution

Claimed: (i) a general plug-in dual-path framework for any encoder-decoder network; (ii) optimal-transport cross-view alignment enabling distribution-level matching of unpaired data; (iii) two-layer decoupling with CMI constraints restricting transfer to the shared space; (iv) persistent-homology topological consistency as an unsupervised prior against overfitting [p. 2]. My reading: the individual ingredients are adapted from known tools (Sinkhorn OT, CMI disentanglement, differentiable persistence); the novelty is their combination into a backbone-agnostic wrapper and the empirical claim of data-efficiency, which is the paper's real selling point rather than any single module.

## 4. Experiments and results

**Data.** PME: 429 patients, 5 centers, apical 4-chamber long-axis and papillary-muscle short-axis, end-systole and end-diastole frames, 858 images per view, left-ventricular myocardium labels [p. 8]. FLARE2023: 581 2D slices per view from 3D CT after liver-size/tumor filtering [p. 8]. MSD: 172 images per view, anterior hippocampus [p. 8]. Patient-level split: 20% independent test, remaining data in 5-fold CV; 512x512 crops; augmentation only on training folds [pp. 8-9].

**Setup.** PyTorch 1.12, Adam, lr 2e-4 cosine-annealed to 1e-5, batch 2, 100 epochs, backbone frozen for 30 epochs, τ=0.2, T=2.0, α=0.1, β_s=β_l=0.05, two RTX 4090s [p. 8]. Metrics: DSC, IoU, HD95, ASD, averaged over five optimal models on the test set [p. 8].

**Main comparison.** 24 encoder-decoder backbones as single-path (SP) baselines vs. their DPIF dual-path (DP) variants. Reported: all DP variants improved; average DSC gain 13.33% (long axis) and 8.97% (short axis) across the three datasets; largest average gain 19.2% on hippocampus long axis; RollingUNet best at 57.57% DSC gain on hippocampus long axis; average HD95 reduced by 4.27 (long) and 2.38 (short); a few models such as SCSEUNet showed slight HD95 degradation [p. 10]. Table 1 (PME) is legible: e.g., UNet long axis DSC 0.7417 -> 0.8125 (+9.55%), UMNet 0.8058 -> 0.8519 (+5.72%) [p. 9]. Tables 2-3 (FLARE2023, MSD) are badly garbled in the supplied text (interleaved rows/columns), so per-model numbers there cannot be reliably attributed; I do not reconstruct them [p. 11].

**Multi-view baselines.** Five methods (AMDANet, CoBioNet, DSM, MSMVNet, PGRNet) all on UMNet backbone, same split [p. 12]. DP-UMNet leads on all views: PME long 0.8519 vs SP 0.8058 (+5.72%), short 0.8495 (+6.40%); FLARE long 0.9824 (+5.77%), short 0.9503 (+1.05%); MSD long 0.9124 (+0.52%), short 0.9182 (+0.11%). Most competitors underperform SP-UMNet, with MSMVNet and CoBioNet worst (e.g., MSMVNet MSD long -30.59%) [p. 12]. Note the MSD short-axis DP HD95 of 1.9608 looks anomalous relative to its SP value of 6.0197 and to the ASD, and the text does not discuss it.

**Ablation (PME, UMNet).** Baseline long-axis DSC 0.8058. Decoupling alone 0.8082 (+0.30%); Sinkhorn alone 0.8245 (+2.32%); adaptive weights alone 0.8073 (+0.19%); topology alone 0.8152 (+1.17%); full 0.8519 (+5.72%); short-axis full 0.8495 (+6.40%) [p. 14]. Text states Sinkhorn adds 2% long / 2.24% short and topology adds 1.14% long with HD95 down ~0.39 [p. 14]; the table's topology-only row shows +1.17% and HD95 12.6179 -> 11.2587, a larger drop than the text's figure — an internal inconsistency worth flagging.

**Data-volume study.** Stratified nested subsets of 20/40/60/80% with RollingUNet, UNet, UMNet; fixed test set, 5-fold CV [p. 14]. Gains largest between 20% and 40%; DP models reach full-data SP accuracy below 60% annotation in most cases; DP-RollingUNet at 20% beats full-data SP on PME short axis; thresholds cited: PME ~60%, FLARE2023 ~40%, MSD ~60% [pp. 14-15]. Figure 5 curves are not numerically readable in the text.

**Clinician review.** 3 ultrasound + 3 radiology specialists, 1-5 Likert, 30 cases per view, blinded randomized display [p. 15]. PME short axis 3.49±0.60 vs 3.07±0.67 (Wilcoxon p=0.004, Cliff's δ=0.57), score>=4 rising 24.4%->52.2%; FLARE long p=0.035; MSD long p=0.049; PME long, FLARE short, MSD short non-significant (p=0.647, 0.917, 0.519) [p. 15].

## 5. Assessment

Supported: DPIF improves over its own SP baselines broadly across backbones, and the data-efficiency trend is consistent across three datasets and three backbones. Weak or missing: (a) the main comparison's annotation budget is never stated, so "comparable amounts of data" cannot be verified; (b) single-module ablation gains are small and the topology row conflicts with the text; (c) Tables 2-3 are unreadable here, so the headline 13.33%/8.97% averages cannot be checked; (d) no statistical testing on segmentation metrics, only on reader scores; (e) no compute/latency cost of the dual training reported; (f) the claim of unpaired operation is not tested with deliberately unpaired data. Authors' stated limitations: only two views supported, and the differentiable persistence approximation may miss subtle topology [p. 17].

## 6. Reproduction

Reported: PyTorch 1.12; Adam; lr 2e-4 -> 1e-5 cosine; batch 2; 100 epochs; backbone frozen 30 epochs; τ=0.2; T=2.0; α=0.1; β_s=β_l=0.05; 512x512; patient-level 20% test + 5-fold CV; augmentation only on training folds; two RTX 4090 [pp. 8-9]. Unreported: λ_d, λ_t, λ_k values (the α/β symbols in Sec. 4.3 do not map cleanly onto Eq. 7's λ's); Sinkhorn ε and iteration count; Gaussian smoothing scales; exact layers where ODI is inserted; CMI estimator used; number of annotated cases in the main comparison; code/data availability. These must be obtained from the authors or code release.

title: Supervision-Adaptive Curriculum and Guarded Anti-Curriculum Learning for Dense Prediction
summary: Curriculum learning orders samples by difficulty, but difficulty alone does not establish supervision reliability for dense prediction. Easy samples can expose shortcuts, hard samples can be informative, and noisy or ambiguous samples can mislead training. Building on our conference method CurriSeg, we present PaceShift, a stabilize-then-challenge paradigm combining supervision-adaptive curriculum selection with guarded spectral post-training. A learning-dynamics view motivates separating supervision reliability from temporal update value and applying spectral challenges after stabilization. The first phase estimates reliability from available supervision, augmentation consistency, model disagreement, and prediction certainty. Temporal statistics guide sample weighting, while pixel-uncertainty weights reduce the early influence of uncertain regions. The second phase ranks predictions from multiple spectral views using supervision agreement, robustness, reference consistency, and penalties. A pairwise preference objective measured against the frozen Phase-I reference, together with an anchor, refines the prediction. The framework supports full, weak, semi-supervised, and model-derived supervision. Experiments across context-entangled content segmentation (CECS), broader dense-prediction tasks, and foundation-model and cross-modal adaptations show accuracy gains. Targeted diagnostics indicate improved pooled calibration and corruption robustness in the evaluated settings. PaceShift preserves the deployed architecture and adds no inference computation. Code will be publicly released.

notes_zh.digest_en: PaceShift is a two-phase training-schedule method for dense prediction that leaves the deployed architecture unchanged and adds no inference cost. Phase I (SA-RCS, epochs 1–60) replaces ground-truth-mask difficulty with a supervision-adaptive reliability score ρi built from four cues (supervision agreement, augmentation consistency, model disagreement, prediction certainty), combines it with temporal sample weighting and pixel-uncertainty weighting, and selects samples by a percentile curriculum. Phase II (SBFT-P, epochs 61–70) applies a multi-radius spectral low-pass challenge (r ∈ {0.90, 0.95, 1.00}), scores candidates with a supervision-adaptive guard, and fine-tunes with a DPO-style pairwise preference loss plus a KL anchor to the frozen Phase-I model. Reported gains span CECS (COD, PIS, TOD, CDD), broader dense prediction, weak/semi-supervision, foundation-model adapters, and VLM/reference-guided segmentation, with mean relative gains of roughly 3–5% on COD and improved pooled ECE (0.019→0.011 on COD10K) and corruption retention. Evidence is strongest for CECS and unreliable-supervision settings; the broader-task experiments do not isolate each phase.

# PaceShift：面向密集预测的监督自适应课程与受守卫的反课程学习——阅读笔记

## 1. 问题与动机

论文针对密集预测（逐像素标注），主张进展多来自架构，而*训练信号*的可靠性及其被消费的顺序研究不足 [p. 1]。作者聚焦上下文纠缠内容分割（CECS：伪装目标检测、透明目标检测、隐蔽缺陷检测，以及作为相关低对比度任务的金标准息肉分割），其中目标与背景共享低层统计特性 [p. 1]。

三点观察构成动机 [pp. 1–2]：（i）难度≠学习价值——样本“容易”可能源于残余高频纹理对比，易到难课程会强化脆弱捷径；（ii）难样本具有歧义——高误差可能来自有信息量的难度，也可能来自不可靠监督（弱标注、标签漂移、歧义）；（iii）置信度≠可靠性——不确定的边界像素会主导早期梯度，奖励置信度会强化错误并损害校准。作者报告：在匹配预算下，朴素易到难排序并不优于随机排序，且朴素易优先训练会提高对高频扰动的敏感性 [p. 1]。

前作 CurriSeg（ICML 2026）使用稠密掩码 IoU 难度、时序加权、像素不确定性加权和单半径频谱盲微调（SBFT）。其局限是：难度分数需要稠密掩码（无法用于弱监督、半监督或模型派生监督），且单半径频谱阶段缺乏评估备选预测的机制 [p. 2]。

## 2. 方法

**设定。** 数据集 D = {(x_i, s_i)}；s_i 为稠密掩码（全监督）、稀疏线索如涂鸦/点/框（弱监督），或仅对已标注子集 D_L 有掩码（半监督）[p. 3]。模型 f_θ 不变，PaceShift 只重组训练。训练共 T 轮：第一阶段（SA-RCS）第 1…T_c 轮，第二阶段（SBFT-P）第 T_c+1…T 轮 [p. 3]。

**第一阶段——监督自适应难度。** 难度 d_i = 1 − ρ_i，ρ_i ∈ [0,1] 为四个归一化线索的凸组合 [式 (2)，p. 5]：监督一致性 s_i^sup（全监督下与 GT 的 IoU；弱监督下满足线索比例，点监督取点线索满足度与冻结 SAM3 提议一致性的平均；无标注样本取 EMA 教师或基础模型一致性）；增强一致性 s_i^cons（两次随机增强预测逆变换后 1−IoU 的平均分歧）；模型一致性 1−s̄_i^dis（MC dropout 或集成分歧）；预测确定性 1−s̄_i^ent（1 减去图像级平均归一化像素熵）。权重不按场景调参：单一信任水平 τ_trust 令 a_sup = τ_trust，其余 (1−τ_trust) 按固定模板 π = (0.4, 0.4, 0.2) 分配给一致性、分歧、熵 [式 (2)，表 I，p. 5]。预设：τ_trust = 0.7（稠密人工掩码）、0.4（稀疏人工线索）、0.3（模型派生）。

**预热与百分位课程。** 前 T_w = 10 轮使用全部样本；之后活跃集 S_t 包含 d_i 低于百分位阈值 Per(·, p(t)) 的样本，p(t) 从 p_min = 0.6 线性升至 T_c 时的 1.0 [式 (3)，p. 5]。

**时序样本加权。** 在 K = 5 个刷新检查点（每 H = 10 轮）保存难度历史 B_i = {d_i^(1),…,d_i^(K)}，计算均值 μ_i 与方差 σ_i² [式 (4)，p. 5]。最小-最大归一化后，ω_i^μ = 1−μ̃_i，ω_i^σ = 4σ̃_i²(1−σ̃_i²)，这是无参数的抛物线型中方差偏好，同时抑制已稳定与高度不稳定样本 [式 (5)，p. 5]。最终权重 ω_i = w_min + (1−w_min)ω_i^μ ω_i^σ ω_i^out，w_min = 0.1，离群因子 ω_i^out = 1−μ̃_i(1−σ̃_i²) [式 (6)，p. 5]。

**像素不确定性加权（PUE）。** 令 p = σ(ŷ)，归一化熵 E_{h,w} = −p log₂p − (1−p)log₂(1−p) [式 (7)]；像素权重 W_{h,w}(t) = w_min + (1−w_min)(1−β(t)E_{h,w})，β(t) = max(0, 1−t/T_c) [式 (8)，p. 6]。权重从计算图中分离；第二阶段 β = 0，故 W = 1。

**统一损失。** L_curr = ω_i L_seg^w(ŷ_i, t_i, W_i) [式 (9)，p. 6]，其中 L_seg^w 在全监督下为加权 BCE+IoU，弱监督下为对应涂鸦/点/框损失，无标注样本为熵门控伪标签损失。无监督像素对 L_seg^w 贡献为零，但仍进入一致性与熵线索。

**第二阶段——多半径频谱挑战。** 用圆形频域掩码 M_r 对输入低通，r ∈ {0.90, 0.95, 1.00} [式 (10)，p. 6]；r = 1.00 为恒等（干净）视图。每个视图产生分离的候选掩码 m_i^r = sg[σ(f_θ(x̃_i^r))]。

**守卫。** Q(m) = τ_trust Q_sup(m)[Q_rob(m)+Q_cons(m)] + (1−τ_trust)/2 − ε[Q_deg(m)+Q_unc(m)] [式 (11)，p. 6]，其中 Q_sup 为对可用监督的正确性，Q_rob 为与其他半径候选的平均一致性，Q_cons 为与冻结第一阶段参考 θ₀ 的一致性，Q_deg 为退化惩罚（全背景、面积坍缩、过度平滑），Q_unc 为平均熵，ε = 0.1。偏好/非偏好掩码为各半径上的 argmax/argmin [式 (12)，p. 6]。

**偏好目标。** 令 ℓ_θ(m|x) 为像素平均对数似然 [式 (13)]，Δℓ_θ(m) = ℓ_θ(m) − ℓ_θ₀(m)，L_pref = −log σ(Δℓ_θ(m⁺) − Δℓ_θ(m⁻)) [式 (14)，p. 7]，在干净输入上计算。由于 ℓ 对掩码仿射，等价于 logit 边际形式 (1/|Ω|)Σ_j (m_j⁺ − m_j⁻)Δz_j [式 (15)]。锚项 L_anc = KL(p_θ₀(x_i) ‖ p_θ(x_i)) [式 (16)] 与保留的 SBFT 项 L_SBFT = L_wBCE(p̃_i, t_i) + L_wIoU(p̃_i, t_i)，p̃_i = σ(f_θ(x̃_i^0.95)) [式 (17)]，构成 L_post = L_SBFT + L_pref + λ_anc L_anc，λ_anc = 0.1 [式 (18)，p. 7]。全监督下去掉偏好与锚项、取 r = 0.95 即恢复会议版 SBFT。

**默认设置。** Adam (β₁, β₂) = (0.9, 0.999)；H = 10；T_c = 60，T = 70；p_min = 0.6；标准 CECS 实验输入 352×352；跨任务实验保留各宿主的分辨率、优化器、学习率、批大小、增强与预算，并按比例缩放阶段边界 [pp. 7–8]。

## 3. 贡献

作者主张 [p. 2]：（1）学习动力学视角，将监督可靠性与时序更新价值分离，并把 SBFT 视为顺序重要的稳定后频率瓶颈；（2）可在全监督、弱监督、半监督和模型派生监督下使用的监督自适应课程选择；（3）带偏好守卫的受守卫反课程后训练（SBFT-P），SBFT 为其特例；（4）系统验证与诊断。我的解读：核心新意是可靠性分数 ρ_i（四线索、单一信任标量）与受守卫多半径偏好阶段；时序加权与 PUE 是对 CurriSeg 的改进，DPO 式目标是将已有思想适配到稠密掩码。

## 4. 实验与结果

**COD（表 II，p. 8）。** 四种骨干（ResNet50、Res2Net50、PVT V2、DINO V2-L）与四个检测器（FEDER、FSEL、RUN、NUN），数据集 CHAMELEON、CAMO、COD10K、NC4K；指标 M↓、F_β↑、E_φ↑、S_α↑。例：RUN++（ResNet50）COD10K 为 M 0.027、F_β 0.775、E_φ 0.926、S_α 0.838，RUN 为 0.030/0.747/0.903/0.827；NUN++ 配 DINO V2-L 总体最强（COD10K 0.012/0.891/0.982/0.910）。平均相对提升 3.3–5.3%。

**开销（表 III，p. 8）。** 每轮时间约增 20%（FEDER 1.00×→1.18×），但总墙钟时间更低，因为课程配方用 70 轮而 FEDER 官方为 100 轮；推理不变。

**显著性（表 IV，p. 9）。** COD10K（ResNet50）五次配对运行：+ 与 ++ 在三个指标上均以 p < 0.001 优于基线；++ 在 F_β 与 E_φ 上以 p < 0.01 优于 +，但 S_α 增益（0.002）不显著。

**其他 CECS（表 V–VII，p. 9）。** PIS（PVT V2）、TOD（PVT V2）、CDS2K 上的 CDD；CDD 相对增益约 7.7–7.9%，为四任务中最大。

**架构泛化（表 VIII，p. 10）。** 十二个检测器的十三种配置；每种配置提升 3.8–6.5%，且 PaceShift 在全部十三行超过 CurriSeg。

**更广任务族（表 IX，p. 10）。** IRSTD-1k（IRSAM IoU 73.7→75.5）、SBU（Spider BER 0.040→0.038）、ISIC 2018（DconnNet DSC 90.4→90.7）、RETOUCH（87.7→87.5，即 CurriSeg 低于基线，PaceShift 恢复）、DIS-VD、DUTS-TE、ADE20K（CGRSeg mIoU 45.5→46.8）、COCO（M2Form AP 38.0→38.6）。

**数据中心方法比较（表 X、图 5，p. 10）。** 在线策略：朴素损失课程反而变差（Δ 1.23↓）；Dyn-Unc 1.55↑、TDDS 2.43↑、CurriSeg 2.10↑、仅 SA-RCS 2.03↑、PaceShift 2.43↑（S_α 0.838）。核心集：PaceShift 诊断在 20% 保留率有竞争力，在 40–80% 最佳。

**不完整监督（表 XI–XIII，p. 11）。** 点监督 SEE/SCALER（如 SEE++ Δ 4.94↑ 对 SEE+ 2.45↑）；1/16 半监督 CoSOD（Δ 5.06↑ 对 2.01↑）。伪标签分诊：ρ_i 标记 P/R 0.769、保留质量 0.827、AUROC 0.827，置信度过滤为 0.589/0.801/0.682；无外部提议的 ρ_i 仍优于所有非外部基线。

**基础模型适配器（表 XIV，p. 11）。** SAM-、SAM2-、SAM3-Adapter 均提升（如 SAM3-Adapter 0.015/0.883/0.965/0.927 → 0.013/0.901/0.975/0.932，Δ 4.24↑）。

**VLM/参考引导（表 XV–XVII，p. 12）。** WeCLIP VOC mIoU 76.4→77.3；ExCEL 78.4→79.2；OVCamo 上 OVCoser/COCUS；R2C7K 上 R2CNet 与 RefOnce。

**消融（表 XVIII–XXIII，pp. 13–14）。** 第一阶段全因子：选择单独最强，时序加权带来较小但一致的增益，PUE 单独较弱但互补。排序：随机≈不选择；损失/置信度排序不稳定；在线 SA-RCS 最佳（0.019/0.824/0.952/0.881）。第二阶段：完整 SBFT-P 最佳（0.017/0.835/0.962/0.888，S_α^c 0.831，ECE 0.011，GT-CAG 0.036）；置信度偏好会扩大 GT-CAG；去掉锚项损失精度。阶段顺序：挑战优先显著低于标准训练；反转阶段可恢复大部分但仍在标准训练之下。信任预设优于均匀与错配信任；±20% 扰动稳定。

**鲁棒性与校准（图 7、表 XXIV，p. 15）。** 在每个非零严重度上 PaceShift 的 S_α 保留率高于 CurriSeg；COD10K 上 ECE 0.019→0.011（CurriSeg 0.016）；温度缩放 ECE 略低，但 PaceShift 边界差距更小、错误像素置信度更低。

**机制分析（表 XXV–XXVII，pp. 15–16）。** ρ_i 五分位显示伪标签质量单调（首尾 IoU 差 32.2 点，Spearman 0.64）；ω_i 与优化器条件对齐代理相关性最强（0.53），瞬时损失为负（−0.25）；守卫相对最佳单线索将 regret 减半；在未见过的 0.70 截止频率上，PaceShift 相对标准训练将高频移除与噪声敏感性分别降低 43% 与 45%。

## 5. 评价

有支持的结论：多检测器/骨干与多监督场景下的精度提升；在所评估设置中池化校准与腐蚀保留率改善；无推理开销。作者声明的局限 [p. 16]：频谱干预在目标与背景共享低层统计时最有用；更广实验未逐阶段隔离；极小目标在衰减下可能丢失有用证据；残余失败包括重叠实例与严重遮挡；不完整监督收益依赖外部教师/提议质量；第二阶段增加少量训练计算。缺失/不清：表 II、IV–VII、XI–XII、XIV–XVII、XX–XXIII 在提供文本中部分乱码，部分数字无法核实；声称不做逐数据集调参，但信任预设为手工设定；统计检验仅限 COD10K。

## 6. 复现

已报告：PyTorch、Adam (0.9, 0.999)；H = 10；T_w = 10；T_c = 60；T = 70；p_min = 0.6；w_min = 0.1；ε = 0.1；λ_anc = 0.1；半径 {0.90, 0.95, 1.00}；K = 5 个刷新检查点；标准 CECS 输入 352×352；标准翻转/裁剪/光度增强；信任预设 0.7/0.4/0.3；表 III 开销测量批大小为 2。正文未报告：学习率、权重衰减、弱/半监督损失的具体系数、SAM3 提示细节以及各任务完整调度（推迟到未提供的补充材料）。

# PaceShift: Supervision-Adaptive Curriculum and Guarded Anti-Curriculum Learning for Dense Prediction — Reading Notes

## 1. Problem and motivation

The paper targets dense prediction (per-pixel labeling) and argues that progress has been mostly architectural, while the *training signal* — its reliability and the order in which it is consumed — is underexplored [p. 1]. The authors focus on context-entangled content segmentation (CECS: camouflaged object detection, transparent object detection, concealed defect detection, plus polyp segmentation as a related low-contrast task), where objects share low-level statistics with the background [p. 1].

Three observations motivate the design [pp. 1–2]: (i) difficulty ≠ learning value — easy samples may be easy because of residual high-frequency texture contrast, so easy-first curricula can reinforce a fragile shortcut; (ii) hard samples are ambiguous — high error may reflect informative difficulty or unreliable supervision (weak labels, label drift, ambiguity); (iii) confidence ≠ reliability — uncertain boundary pixels can dominate early gradients, and rewarding confidence can reinforce errors and hurt calibration. The authors report that under a matched budget naive easy-to-hard ordering performs no better than random, and that naive easy-first training increases sensitivity to high-frequency perturbations [p. 1].

The predecessor, CurriSeg (ICML 2026), used dense-mask IoU difficulty, temporal weighting, pixel-uncertainty weighting, and single-radius spectral-blindness fine-tuning (SBFT). Its limitations: the difficulty score required dense masks (so it could not handle weak, semi-supervised, or model-derived supervision), and its single-radius spectral stage had no mechanism to judge alternative predictions [p. 2].

## 2. Method

**Setup.** Dataset D = {(x_i, s_i)}; s_i is a dense mask (full supervision), a sparse cue such as scribble/point/box (weak), or a mask only for a labeled subset D_L (semi-supervised) [p. 3]. The model f_θ is unchanged; PaceShift only reorganizes training. Training runs T epochs: Phase I (SA-RCS) epochs 1…T_c, Phase II (SBFT-P) epochs T_c+1…T [p. 3].

**Phase I — supervision-adaptive difficulty.** Difficulty is d_i = 1 − ρ_i, where ρ_i ∈ [0,1] is a convex combination of four normalized cues [Eq. (2), p. 5]: supervision agreement s_i^sup (IoU with GT under full supervision; satisfied-cue ratio under weak supervision, with point supervision averaging point-cue satisfaction and agreement with a frozen SAM3 proposal; EMA-teacher or foundation-model agreement for unlabeled data); augmentation consistency s_i^cons (1 − mean disagreement between two stochastic augmentations, inverse-warped, measured by 1−IoU); model agreement 1−s̄_i^dis (Monte-Carlo dropout or ensemble disagreement); prediction certainty 1−s̄_i^ent (1 − image-level mean normalized pixel entropy). Weights are not tuned per regime: a single trust level τ_trust sets a_sup = τ_trust and the residual (1−τ_trust) is split by a fixed template π = (0.4, 0.4, 0.2) over consistency, disagreement, entropy [Eq. (2), Table I, p. 5]. Presets: τ_trust = 0.7 (dense human mask), 0.4 (sparse human cue), 0.3 (model-derived).

**Warm-up and percentile curriculum.** For the first T_w = 10 epochs all samples are used; afterwards the active set S_t contains samples with d_i below the percentile threshold Per(·, p(t)), with p(t) rising linearly from p_min = 0.6 to 1.0 by T_c [Eq. (3), p. 5].

**Temporal sample weighting.** At K = 5 refresh checkpoints (every H = 10 epochs) the difficulty history B_i = {d_i^(1),…,d_i^(K)} is stored; mean μ_i and variance σ_i² are computed [Eq. (4), p. 5]. After min-max normalization, ω_i^μ = 1−μ̃_i and ω_i^σ = 4σ̃_i²(1−σ̃_i²), a parameter-free parabolic mid-variance preference that suppresses both already-stable and highly unstable samples [Eq. (5), p. 5]. The final weight is ω_i = w_min + (1−w_min)ω_i^μ ω_i^σ ω_i^out with w_min = 0.1 and an outlier factor ω_i^out = 1−μ̃_i(1−σ̃_i²) [Eq. (6), p. 5].

**Pixel uncertainty weighting (PUE).** With p = σ(ŷ), normalized entropy E_{h,w} = −p log₂p − (1−p)log₂(1−p) [Eq. (7)]; the pixel weight is W_{h,w}(t) = w_min + (1−w_min)(1−β(t)E_{h,w}) with β(t) = max(0, 1−t/T_c) [Eq. (8), p. 6]. Weights are detached from the graph; in Phase II β = 0 so W = 1.

**Unified loss.** L_curr = ω_i L_seg^w(ŷ_i, t_i, W_i) [Eq. (9), p. 6], where L_seg^w is weighted BCE+IoU (full), the corresponding scribble/point/box loss (weak), or an entropy-gated pseudo-label loss (unlabeled). Unsupervised pixels contribute zero to L_seg^w but still enter the consistency/entropy cues.

**Phase II — multi-radius spectral challenge.** Inputs are low-passed with a circular frequency mask M_r for r ∈ {0.90, 0.95, 1.00} [Eq. (10), p. 6]; r = 1.00 is the identity (clean) view. Each view yields a detached candidate mask m_i^r = sg[σ(f_θ(x̃_i^r))].

**Guard.** Q(m) = τ_trust Q_sup(m)[Q_rob(m)+Q_cons(m)] + (1−τ_trust)/2 − ε[Q_deg(m)+Q_unc(m)] [Eq. (11), p. 6], with Q_sup correctness against the available supervision, Q_rob mean agreement with other radii, Q_cons agreement with the frozen Phase-I reference θ₀, Q_deg a degeneration penalty (all-background, area collapse, over-smoothing), Q_unc mean entropy, and ε = 0.1. Preferred/dispreferred masks are the argmax/argmin over radii [Eq. (12), p. 6].

**Preference objective.** With ℓ_θ(m|x) the pixel-averaged log-likelihood [Eq. (13)], Δℓ_θ(m) = ℓ_θ(m) − ℓ_θ₀(m), and L_pref = −log σ(Δℓ_θ(m⁺) − Δℓ_θ(m⁻)) [Eq. (14), p. 7], evaluated on the clean input. Because ℓ is affine in the mask, this equals a logit-margin form (1/|Ω|)Σ_j (m_j⁺ − m_j⁻)Δz_j [Eq. (15)]. An anchor L_anc = KL(p_θ₀(x_i) ‖ p_θ(x_i)) [Eq. (16)] and the retained SBFT term L_SBFT = L_wBCE(p̃_i, t_i) + L_wIoU(p̃_i, t_i) with p̃_i = σ(f_θ(x̃_i^0.95)) [Eq. (17)] give L_post = L_SBFT + L_pref + λ_anc L_anc, λ_anc = 0.1 [Eq. (18), p. 7]. Under full supervision, dropping preference and anchor with r = 0.95 recovers conference SBFT.

**Defaults.** Adam (β₁, β₂) = (0.9, 0.999); H = 10; T_c = 60, T = 70; p_min = 0.6; inputs 352×352 for canonical CECS experiments; cross-task experiments keep each host's resolution, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, augmentation and budget, scaling phase boundaries proportionally [pp. 7–8].

## 3. Contribution

Authors' claims [p. 2]: (1) a learning-dynamics view separating supervision reliability from temporal update value and treating SBFT as a post-stabilization frequency bottleneck whose order matters; (2) supervision-adaptive curriculum selection usable under full, weak, semi-supervised and model-derived supervision; (3) guarded anti-curriculum post-training (SBFT-P) with a preference guard, recovering SBFT as a special case; (4) systematic validation and diagnostics. My interpretation: the core novelty is the reliability score ρ_i (four cues, one trust scalar) and the guarded multi-radius preference stage; the temporal weighting and PUE are refinements of CurriSeg, and the DPO-style objective is an adaptation of an existing idea to dense masks.

## 4. Experiments and results

**COD (Table II, p. 8).** Four backbones (ResNet50, Res2Net50, PVT V2, DINO V2-L) and four detectors (FEDER, FSEL, RUN, NUN) on CHAMELEON, CAMO, COD10K, NC4K; metrics M↓, F_β↑, E_φ↑, S_α↑. Example: RUN++ (ResNet50) COD10K M 0.027, F_β 0.775, E_φ 0.926, S_α 0.838 vs RUN 0.030/0.747/0.903/0.827; NUN++ with DINO V2-L is strongest overall (COD10K 0.012/0.891/0.982/0.910). Mean relative gains 3.3–5.3%.

**Cost (Table III, p. 8).** ~20% higher per-epoch time (FEDER 1.00×→1.18×), but lower total wall-clock because curriculum recipes use 70 epochs vs. e.g. FEDER's 100; inference unchanged.

**Significance (Table IV, p. 9).** Five paired runs on COD10K (ResNet50): both + and ++ beat baseline at p < 0.001 on all three metrics; ++ beats + on F_β and E_φ at p < 0.01, but S_α gains (0.002) are not significant.

**Other CECS (Tables V–VII, p. 9).** PIS (PVT V2), TOD (PVT V2), CDD on CDS2K; CDD relative gains ~7.7–7.9%, the largest of the four tasks.

**Architectures (Table VIII, p. 10).** Thirteen configurations of twelve detectors; every configuration improves within 3.8–6.5%, and PaceShift exceeds CurriSeg on all thirteen rows.

**Broader families (Table IX, p. 10).** IRSTD-1k (IRSAM IoU 73.7→75.5), SBU (Spider BER 0.040→0.038), ISIC 2018 (DconnNet DSC 90.4→90.7), RETOUCH (87.7→87.5, i.e., CurriSeg below baseline, PaceShift recovers), DIS-VD, DUTS-TE, ADE20K (CGRSeg mIoU 45.5→46.8), COCO (M2Form AP 38.0→38.6).

**Data-centric comparisons (Table X, Fig. 5, p. 10).** Online: naive loss curriculum hurts (Δ 1.23↓); Dyn-Unc 1.55↑, TDDS 2.43↑, CurriSeg 2.10↑, SA-RCS only 2.03↑, PaceShift 2.43↑ (S_α 0.838). Coreset: PaceShift's diagnostic is competitive at 20% retention and best at 40–80%.

**Incomplete supervision (Tables XI–XIII, p. 11).** Point supervision with SEE/SCALER (e.g., SEE++ Δ 4.94↑ vs SEE+ 2.45↑); semi-supervision 1/16 with CoSOD (Δ 5.06↑ vs 2.01↑). Pseudo-label triage: ρ_i flagging P/R 0.769, retained quality 0.827, AUROC 0.827 vs confidence filter 0.589/0.801/0.682; ρ_i without external proposal still beats all non-external baselines.

**Foundation adapters (Table XIV, p. 11).** SAM-, SAM2-, SAM3-Adapters all improve (e.g., SAM3-Adapter 0.015/0.883/0.965/0.927 → 0.013/0.901/0.975/0.932, Δ 4.24↑).

**VLM/reference (Tables XV–XVII, p. 12).** WeCLIP 76.4→77.3 VOC mIoU; ExCEL 78.4→79.2; OVCoser/COCUS on OVCamo; R2CNet and RefOnce on R2C7K.

**Ablations (Tables XVIII–XXIII, pp. 13–14).** Phase-I factorial: selection strongest alone, temporal weighting adds a smaller consistent gain, PUE weak alone but complementary. Ordering: random ≈ no selection; loss/confidence rankings inconsistent; online SA-RCS best (0.019/0.824/0.952/0.881). Phase II: full SBFT-P best (0.017/0.835/0.962/0.888, S_α^c 0.831, ECE 0.011, GT-CAG 0.036); confidence preference widens GT-CAG; removing the anchor costs accuracy. Phase order: challenge-first falls below standard training; reversed phases recover much but stay below. Trust presets beat uniform and mismatched trust; ±20% perturbations are stable.

**Robustness/calibration (Fig. 7, Table XXIV, p. 15).** PaceShift retains more S_α than CurriSeg at every nonzero severity; ECE 0.019→0.011 on COD10K (CurriSeg 0.016); temperature scaling reaches slightly lower ECE but PaceShift gives smaller boundary gap and lower confidence on incorrect pixels.

**Mechanism (Tables XXV–XXVII, pp. 15–16).** ρ_i quintiles show monotone pseudo-label quality (32.2-point top-bottom IoU gap, Spearman 0.64); ω_i has the strongest correlation with the optimizer-conditioned alignment proxy (0.53) while instantaneous loss is negative (−0.25); guard halves regret vs. best single cue; at an unseen cutoff 0.70, PaceShift reduces high-frequency-removal and noise sensitivity by 43% and 45% vs. standard training.

## 5. Assessment

Supported: accuracy gains across many detectors/backbones and supervision regimes; improved pooled calibration and corruption retention in the evaluated settings; no inference cost. Limitations stated by authors [p. 16]: spectral intervention is most useful when targets and backgrounds share low-level statistics; broader experiments do not isolate each phase; tiny objects may lose useful evidence under attenuation; residual failures include overlapping instances and heavy occlusion; incomplete-supervision gains depend on external teacher/proposal quality; Phase II adds modest training compute. Missing/unclear: several tables (II, IV–VII, XI–XII, XIV–XVII, XX–XXIII) are partially garbled in the supplied text, so some numbers could not be verified; no per-dataset tuning is claimed, but the trust presets are hand-set; statistical tests are limited to COD10K.

## 6. Reproduction

Reported: PyTorch, Adam (0.9, 0.999); H = 10; T_w = 10; T_c = 60; T = 70; p_min = 0.6; w_min = 0.1; ε = 0.1; λ_anc = 0.1; radii {0.90, 0.95, 1.00}; K = 5 refresh checkpoints; 352×352 inputs for canonical CECS; standard flip/crop/photometric augmentation; trust presets 0.7/0.4/0.3; batch size 2 in Table III cost measurements. Not reported in the main text: learning rate, weight decay, exact loss coefficients for weak/semi regimes, SAM3 prompt details, and full per-task schedules (deferred to the Supp., which is not supplied).

title: Really Need Recursion? Revisiting One-pass Registration with Multi-level Multi-space Contextual Guidance
journal_ref: Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention -- MICCAI 2026, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16889, pp. 279-289, Springer (2027)
summary: Deformable image registration is a fundamental challenge in medical image analysis. Recent deep learning-based methods typically adopt either one-pass architectures that complete registration in a single network iteration, or recursive architectures that refine registration through multiple passes. While recursive methods often improve accuracy, they incur substantial computational overhead and slower inference speed. In this paper, we challenge the necessity of recursion for high-performance deformable registration and propose M2CG, a one-pass registration network with Multi-level Multi-space Contextual Guidance. It performs multi-step progressive pyramid registration within a single iteration, guided at each step by contextual cues from three levels (previous, current, and subsequent steps) and four spaces (image space, image feature space, segmentation space, and segmentation feature space). Our M2CG supports both unsupervised (without any labels) and semi-supervised (with segmentation labels for partial training data) registration, and has achieved state-of-the-art performance across two well-benchmarked inter-/intra-patient medical registration tasks with eight public datasets. Our findings suggest that the current reliance on recursion may stem from the absence of sufficient contextual cues that comprehensively characterize the remaining distance to the target alignment.

notes_zh.digest_en: M2CG is a one-pass pyramid registration network that replaces recursion with multi-level (previous/current/subsequent) and multi-space (image, image-feature, segmentation, segmentation-feature) contextual guidance. On brain (OASIS/Mindboggle/Buckner) and cardiac (ACDC) benchmarks it reports the best DSC in both unsupervised and semi-supervised settings (e.g., OASIS 0.815 unsup / 0.862 semi; ACDC 0.810 / 0.872) at one-pass runtime (0.32 s brain, 0.04 s cardiac). Ablations show each cue contributes, and adding recursion (network/decoder/pyramid-scale) yields only marginal DSC gains while roughly doubling cost and increasing negative Jacobian determinants, supporting the authors' claim that recursion's benefit shrinks when contextual guidance is sufficient.

notes_zh.full_md:
## 1. 问题与动机

可变形医学图像配准通过稠密位移场把浮动图像对齐到固定图像。深度方法分为两类：单次（one-pass）网络（VoxelMorph、TransMorph、NICE-Net 及其后续）与递归/级联网络（RCN、LapIRN、RDN、RDP、ReCorr），后者通过多次传递细化对齐 [p. 2]。递归通常提升精度，但计算与推理时间更高；近期甚至有研究用递归网络作教师蒸馏单次学生网络 [p. 2]。作者指出，少有工作追问递归为何有效。其假设是：在金字塔单次配准中，逐步上下文线索刻画了到目标对齐的剩余距离；线索充分时单次渐进配准即可，否则递归以迭代搜索补偿。作者还提醒递归可能累积误差 [p. 2]。

## 2. 方法

**设定。** 学习 R_θ(I_f, I_m)=φ（位移场），使 I_m∘φ 与 I_f 对齐；输入为单通道灰度三维体数据 [p. 3]。

**编码器。** 固定/浮动图像共享四块编码器（每块两个 3×3×3 卷积，块间步长 2 平均池化），得到四级图像特征金字塔 {IF^{1/2}…IF^{1/8}} [pp. 3–4]。

**分割解码器（仅半监督）。** 从最粗特征开始，上采样前一层特征与预测并融合编码器特征，输出四级掩码金字塔 {S^{1/2}…S^{1/8}} 与分割特征金字塔 {SF^{1/2}…SF^{1/8}}；无监督设置下省略 [p. 4]。

**配准解码器。** 四个尺度由粗到细。每个尺度用四个 Intra-space Correlation Module（IntraCM），通过 3D 相关层加 3×3×3 卷积计算固定图像与中间变形图像在四个空间中的对应关系；Multi-space Integration Module（MultiIM）用四个带稠密残差连接的 3×3×3 卷积融合四空间对应信息与上一尺度上采样特征；配准头预测该尺度 φ^s，用于变形下一尺度的 I_m^{s−1}、S_m^{s−1}、IF_m^{s−1}、SF_m^{s−1} [p. 4]。无监督设置去掉分割相关 IntraCM 与操作 [p. 4]。

**三级引导。** 前一层级=MultiIM 中的上采样特征；当前层级=四个 IntraCM 度量当前到目标的距离；后一层级=图像空间 IntraCM 中的小波分解图像。图像金字塔 {I^{1/2}…I^{1/8}} 由小波变换得到：I^{1/2} 为原图，I^{1/4}、I^{1/8}、I^{1/16} 各为 8 通道分解（LLL 加高频子带）。8 个子带无损且下采样，相当于在当前步“预看”更细尺度细节 [pp. 4–5]。

**损失。** 无监督：L_uns = L_sim + σL_reg，σ=1；L_sim 为负局部 NCC；L_reg 为 φ 的扩散正则 [p. 5]。半监督：L_semi = L_uns + αL_seg + βL_joint，α=β=1；沿用 AutoFuse [19]，采用 Dice+Focal，约束 (i) S_{f/m} 与 L_{f/m}、(ii) L_f 与 L_m∘φ、(iii) L_f 与 S_m∘φ、(iv) S_f 与 L_m∘φ；缺失标签的相关项被剔除，从而混合有/无标签数据 [p. 5]。

## 3. 贡献

作者主张：首次在充分上下文引导下实证检验递归必要性；提出 3 层级×4 空间引导的单次网络，支持无监督与半监督；在两项任务/八个数据集上达到 SOTA [pp. 2–3, 8–9]。我的解读：核心新意在于“后一层级”的小波预看线索，以及在同一骨干上系统加入三种递归变体的受控消融；分割空间线索继承自 AutoFuse 式联合学习 [p. 5]。

## 4. 实验与结果

**数据。** 脑部：OASIS 414 例带分割 MRI，按 314/20/80 划分训练/验证/测试；无标签 ADNI、ABIDE、ADHD、IXI（2,656 无标签 + 314 有标签）用于半监督训练；Mindboggle 与 Buckner 独立测试。心脏：ACDC 官方划分，患者内 ED–ES 配准 [p. 5]。预处理细节引至 [19] [p. 5]。

**训练。** PyTorch，40 GB A100，Adam，学习率 1e-4，批大小 1。脑部共 100k 迭代；无监督随机患者间图像对；半监督先 50k 有标签热启动，再 50k 半标签对（一有标签+一无标签）。心脏共 50k 迭代；无监督先 40k 随机患者内 cine 帧，再 10k ED–ES；半监督先 40k 半标签对（有标签 ED/ES + 无标签非 ED/ES），再 10k ED/ES [p. 6]。

**指标。** 分割标签间 DSC；负雅可比行列式百分比 NJD [p. 6]。

**主要结果（表 1，[p. 7]）。** 无监督 M2CG：OASIS 0.815/1.689、Mindboggle 0.648/1.721、Buckner 0.665/1.814、ACDC 0.810/0.358（DSC/NJD）。半监督：0.862/1.668、0.665/1.698、0.687/1.722、0.872/0.348。无监督最佳单次基线 SACB-Net 为 0.802/0.632/0.653/0.800；最佳递归 ReCorr 为 0.806/0.637/0.657/0.803。半监督最佳基线：DAFF-Net 0.846/0.654/0.668/0.859；ReCorr‡ 0.847/0.648/0.667/0.861。运行时间：M2CG 脑 0.32 s、心脏 0.04 s，递归方法为 0.51–0.79 s。显著性标记（*/†，P<0.05）标在基线一侧，表示相对 M2CG。表中 RDP‡ 的 Mindboggle NJD 写作“1,744”，应为笔误 [p. 7]。

**消融（表 2，[p. 8]）。** 去掉各线索均降低两种设置下的 DSC，例如无监督去掉图像特征空间：OASIS 0.796、Mindboggle 0.612、Buckner 0.629、ACDC 0.790；半监督去掉分割特征空间：0.846/0.652/0.670/0.854。去掉前一层级线索降幅较小且有时不显著（OASIS 无监督 0.810、半监督 0.860）。加入递归：网络递归 DSC 基本不变（OASIS 无监督 0.815、半监督 0.861），但 NJD 明显上升（2.533/2.436）；解码器递归与金字塔尺度递归类似（如金字塔尺度 OASIS 0.816/0.862，NJD 2.376/2.583）。受显存限制递归仅执行两次，已约 2 倍开销 [p. 8]。

## 5. 评价

可支持的结论：M2CG 在两种设置、四个测试集上均优于所列基线且保持单次运行时间；消融与假设内部一致。需注意：(a) 基线以“相同损失”重训 [p. 6]，但调参细节未给出；(b) 递归仅两次，“边际收益”未必适用于更深递归；(c) 仅单模态配准，作者明确限定结论范围并将跨模态/其他解剖部位列为未来工作 [p. 9]；(d) 除 P<0.05 标记外无方差/置信区间与逐例分析；(e) 预处理与数据细节引至 [19]，图 1/2 除图注外无文字描述；(f) 半监督增益可能部分来自 AutoFuse 式联合目标而非引导本身，消融未单独隔离损失。

## 6. 复现

已报告：三维单通道输入；四块编码器（每块 2 个 3×3×3 卷积，步长 2 平均池化）；四个 IntraCM（3D 相关 + 3×3×3 卷积）；MultiIM（四个 3×3×3 卷积 + 稠密残差）；小波 8 子带金字塔；Adam、lr 1e-4、批 1、A100 40 GB；上述迭代计划；σ=α=β=1；负局部 NCC + 扩散正则；分割/联合项用 Dice+Focal。未报告：图像块大小/裁剪、NCC 窗口、扩散权重数值、小波基、通道宽度、相关层实现细节、计时所用推理硬件、基线完整超参、完整预处理（引至 [19]）。

notes_en.full_md:
## 1. Problem and motivation

Deformable medical image registration maps a moving image to a fixed image via a dense displacement field. Deep methods split into one-pass networks (VoxelMorph, TransMorph, NICE-Net and successors) and recursive/cascaded networks (RCN, LapIRN, RDN, RDP, ReCorr) that refine alignment over multiple passes [p. 2]. Recursion tends to improve accuracy but costs more compute and inference time; a recent distillation study even uses a recursive teacher for a one-pass student [p. 2]. The authors argue that few works ask *why* recursion helps. Their hypothesis: for pyramid one-pass registration, step-wise contextual cues characterize the remaining distance to the target; if cues are sufficient, one-pass progressive registration suffices, otherwise recursion compensates by iterative search. They also note recursion may accumulate errors [p. 2].

## 2. Method

**Setup.** Registration learns R_θ(I_f, I_m)=φ, a displacement field; I_m∘φ should align with I_f; inputs are single-channel grayscale 3D volumes [p. 3].

**Encoder.** A shared four-block encoder (each block two 3×3×3 convolutions; average pooling stride 2 between blocks) produces a four-level image feature pyramid {IF^{1/2}…IF^{1/8}} for both fixed and moving images [pp. 3–4].

**Segmentation decoder (semi-supervised only).** Starting from the coarsest feature, it upsamples previous features/predictions and fuses encoder features to output a four-level mask pyramid {S^{1/2}…S^{1/8}} and a segmentation-feature pyramid {SF^{1/2}…SF^{1/8}}. It is omitted in the unsupervised setting [p. 4].

**Registration decoder.** Coarse-to-fine over four scales. At each scale, four Intra-space Correlation Modules (IntraCMs) compute fixed-vs-intermediately-warped correspondence in four spaces via a 3D correlation layer plus 3×3×3 convolutions. A Multi-space Integration Module (MultiIM) fuses the four correspondence maps with upsampled features from the previous scale using four 3×3×3 convolutions with dense-style residual connections. A registration head then predicts φ^s, used to warp I_m^{s−1}, S_m^{s−1}, IF_m^{s−1}, SF_m^{s−1} for the next scale [p. 4]. In the unsupervised setting segmentation-related IntraCMs/operations are dropped [p. 4].

**Three-level guidance.** Previous level = upsampled features in MultiIM; current level = the four IntraCMs measuring current distance to target; subsequent level = wavelet-decomposed images in the image-space IntraCM. The image pyramid {I^{1/2}…I^{1/8}} comes from wavelet transforms: I^{1/2} is the original image, and each of I^{1/4}, I^{1/8}, I^{1/16} is an 8-channel decomposition (LLL plus high-frequency sub-bands). Because 8 sub-bands are lossless and downsampled, they give a “look-ahead” preview of finer-scale details at the current step [pp. 4–5].

**Losses.** Unsupervised: L_uns = L_sim + σL_reg, σ=1; L_sim is negative local NCC; L_reg is a diffusion regularizer on φ [p. 5]. Semi-supervised: L_semi = L_uns + αL_seg + βL_joint, α=β=1; following AutoFuse [19], Dice+Focal losses are used, constraining (i) S_{f/m} vs L_{f/m}, (ii) L_f vs L_m∘φ, (iii) L_f vs S_m∘φ, (iv) S_f vs L_m∘φ; terms involving missing labels are excluded so labeled and unlabeled data can be mixed [p. 5].

## 3. Contribution

Authors' claims: first empirical study of recursion necessity under sufficient contextual guidance; a one-pass network with 3-level × 4-space guidance supporting unsupervised and semi-supervised registration; SOTA on two tasks/eight datasets [pp. 2–3, 8–9]. My interpretation: the core novelty is the *subsequent-level* wavelet look-ahead cue and the systematic ablation that adds three recursion variants to the same backbone — a controlled test of the hypothesis rather than a new architecture family. The segmentation-space cues are inherited from AutoFuse-style joint learning [p. 5].

## 4. Experiments and results

**Data.** Brain: OASIS 414 labeled MRIs split 314/20/80 train/val/test; unlabeled ADNI, ABIDE, ADHD, IXI (2,656 unlabeled + 314 labeled) for semi-supervised training; independent tests on Mindboggle and Buckner. Cardiac: ACDC official split, intra-patient ED–ES registration [p. 5]. Preprocessing details deferred to [19] [p. 5].

**Training.** PyTorch, 40 GB A100, Adam, lr 1e-4, batch size 1. Brain: 100k iterations; unsupervised random inter-patient pairs; semi-supervised 50k labeled warm start then 50k semi-labeled pairs (one labeled + one unlabeled). Cardiac: 50k iterations; unsupervised 40k random intra-patient cine frames then 10k ED–ES; semi-supervised 40k semi-labeled (labeled ED/ES + unlabeled non-ED/ES) then 10k ED/ES [p. 6].

**Metrics.** DSC between segmentation labels; NJD percentage for folding [p. 6].

**Main results (Table 1, [p. 7]).** Unsupervised M2CG: OASIS 0.815/1.689, Mindboggle 0.648/1.721, Buckner 0.665/1.814, ACDC 0.810/0.358 (DSC/NJD). Semi-supervised: 0.862/1.668, 0.665/1.698, 0.687/1.722, 0.872/0.348. Best one-pass unsupervised baseline SACB-Net reaches 0.802/0.632/0.653/0.800; best recursive ReCorr 0.806/0.637/0.657/0.803. Semi-supervised best baselines: DAFF-Net 0.846/0.654/0.668/0.859; ReCorr‡ 0.847/0.648/0.667/0.861. Runtime: M2CG 0.32 s brain, 0.04 s cardiac, versus 0.51–0.79 s for recursive methods. Significance markers (*/†, P<0.05) are attached to baselines relative to M2CG. Note the table contains a typo “1,744” for RDP‡ Mindboggle NJD [p. 7].

**Ablations (Table 2, [p. 8]).** Removing each cue lowers DSC in both settings, e.g., unsupervised w/o image-feature-space contexts: OASIS 0.796, Mindboggle 0.612, Buckner 0.629, ACDC 0.790; semi-supervised w/o segmentation-feature-space: 0.846/0.652/0.670/0.854. Removing previous-level cues gives smaller, sometimes non-significant drops (OASIS 0.810 unsup, 0.860 semi). Adding recursion: network recursion leaves DSC essentially unchanged (OASIS 0.815 unsup, 0.861 semi) but NJD rises sharply (2.533 unsup; 2.436 semi); decoder and pyramid-scale recursion behave similarly (e.g., pyramid-scale OASIS 0.816/0.862, NJD 2.376/2.583). Recursion was run only twice due to GPU memory, already ~2× cost [p. 8].

## 5. Assessment

Supported: M2CG beats listed baselines on all four test sets in both settings with one-pass runtime, and the ablation is internally consistent with the hypothesis. Caveats: (a) comparisons rely on re-training baselines with “the same losses” [p. 6], but details of baseline tuning are not given; (b) recursion was limited to two passes, so “marginal gains” may not hold for deeper recursion; (c) only uni-modal registration is tested — authors explicitly scope the conclusion and flag cross-modal/other anatomies as future work [p. 9]; (d) no statistical detail beyond P<0.05 markers, no variance/CI, no per-case analysis; (e) preprocessing and dataset specifics are delegated to [19], and Fig. 1/2 content is not textually described beyond captions; (f) the semi-supervised gains may partly reflect the AutoFuse-style joint objective rather than guidance alone, since the ablation does not isolate the loss.

## 6. Reproduction

Reported: 3D single-channel inputs; four-block encoder (2×3×3×3 conv per block, stride-2 average pooling); four IntraCMs with 3D correlation + 3×3×3 conv; MultiIM with four 3×3×3 convs and dense residuals; wavelet 8-sub-band pyramid; Adam, lr 1e-4, batch 1, A100 40 GB; iteration schedules as above; σ=α=β=1; negative local NCC + diffusion regularizer; Dice+Focal for segmentation/joint terms. Not reported: patch size/cropping, NCC window, diffusion weight value, wavelet family, channel widths, correlation-layer implementation details, inference hardware for runtime, exact baseline hyperparameters, and full preprocessing (deferred to [19]).

title: Hybrid supervised instance segmentation by learning label noise suppression
summary: To reach top accuracy, current fully supervised instance segmentation methods severely rely on large-scale pixel-wise labeled datasets. They are usually expensive and time-consuming to obtain. Though weakly or semi-supervised methods utilize cheap bounding box labeled, image-level labeled or unlabeled samples to save the labeling cost, their performance is largely sacrificed. To save labeling cost without losing much performance, in this paper, we present a pipeline that can utilize economical bounding box labels and accurate pixel-wise labels in a hybrid way. Specifically, we design two ancillary models to learn label noise suppression and obtain accurate pseudo pixel-wise labels from bounding box labels for training. One is designed to suppress mislabeling between foreground and background, and the other is designed to suppress noise from mislabeling of instances. Moreover, we exploit category-aware spatial attention module, category constraint module, instance constraint module, and self-learning training approach to improve the accuracy of pseudo labels. Experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 and the Cityscapes datasets show that our method can achieve competitive performance with much less labeling cost.

notes_zh.digest_en: The paper proposes a three-stage hybrid-supervision pipeline for instance segmentation that uses a small fraction of pixel-wise labels plus bounding-box labels. Two DeepLabv3+-based ancillary models (semantic and instance) learn to suppress background and instance noise in box labels, aided by a category-aware spatial attention module, category/instance constraint modules, and self-learning. On PASCAL VOC 2012 and Cityscapes, the method outperforms weakly/semi-supervised baselines and approaches fully supervised Mask R-CNN/CenterMask at much lower labeling cost (e.g., 1% pixel-wise labels).
notes_zh.digest_zh: 该论文提出一种三阶段混合监督实例分割流程：仅使用少量像素级标注加大量边界框标注。两个基于 DeepLabv3+ 的辅助模型（语义辅助模型与实例辅助模型）分别学习抑制边界框标签中的背景噪声与实例噪声，并结合类别感知空间注意力模块、类别/实例约束模块与自学习训练。在 PASCAL VOC 2012 与 Cityscapes 上，该方法优于弱监督/半监督基线，并在显著降低标注成本（如仅 1% 像素级标注）的情况下接近全监督 Mask R-CNN/CenterMask 的性能。
notes_zh.full_md:
## 1. 问题与动机
全监督实例分割依赖大规模像素级标注，成本高昂：作者引用绘制一个分割约需 79 秒，而获取一个边界框仅约 7 秒，前者约贵 11.3 倍 [p. 1]。使用图像级或框级标签的弱监督方法虽降低成本，但精度明显下降；作者将其归因于框标签中的两类噪声（图 1）：**背景噪声**（框内背景像素被标为前景）与**实例噪声**（重叠框内像素被错误分配给其他实例）[pp. 1–3]。式 (1) 用概率 q0（背景被误标为前景的比例）和 q1（前景像素被分配给错误实例的比例）形式化这两类噪声 [p. 3]。已有框监督工作依赖手工启发式（GrabCut、MCG）或多示例学习，无法利用像素级标签精炼伪标签 [p. 3]。目标是在保持低标注成本的同时，通过少量干净像素级样本与框标签的混合使用维持精度。

## 2. 方法
流程为三阶段级联（图 2），仅在训练阶段使用；主模型训练后独立运行 [p. 2]。

**第一步——语义辅助模型。** 基于 DeepLabv3+（Xception-65 主干），预测语义分割 Y′ = f_θ(X, h_CASA(B))，在框内分离前景与背景，抑制背景噪声 [p. 4, 式 (2)]。

**第二步——实例辅助模型。** 同样基于 DeepLabv3+，但解码器分为置信度与实例两个分支，总 4× 上采样（两层反卷积，中间接残差块）[p. 4]。采用 Neven 等人的空间嵌入损失。实例分支预测像素偏移图 (o_im, o_in)，得到预测中心 c_im = o_im + e_im、c_in = o_in + e_in [式 (3)]，并预测随实例尺寸/形状自适应的边界 (r_im, r_in)。置信度分支输出逐像素置信度 d_i，d_i ≤ 0.5 视为背景。推理时，在每个类别特定框内取置信度最高的前景像素估计中心与边界；若式 (4) 的高斯距离大于 0.5，则将像素聚类到实例 S_k [p. 4]。输出伪实例标签 Y″ = g_φ(X, h_CASA(B, Y′)) [式 (5)]。

**类别感知空间注意力（CASA）。** 两个 CASA 块分别位于 4× 与 16× 下采样尺度，将框标签与中间分割信息融合进主干特征 [p. 5]。每块含类别分支（全局最大/平均池化 + MLP → 通道注意力 F_c ∈ R^{N×1×1}）与形状分支（1×1 卷积 + sigmoid → 空间注意力 F_s ∈ R^{N×H×W}），并额外用 3×3 卷积强调边界；融合方式为逐元素相乘 [p. 5]。

**类别与实例约束模块。** 类别约束将非重叠框内像素限制为背景或该框类别，去除框外误检 [p. 5]。实例约束在聚类前过滤每个框外的置信度图，防止邻近目标合并 [p. 5]。

**自学习。** 利用框标注图像生成的伪标签优化辅助模型自身，忽略不确定类别像素（最大置信度 < 0.5）与重叠框区域的损失，以避免少量像素标签下的过拟合 [p. 5]。

**损失函数。** 总损失 L_total = λ_conf L_conf + λ_inst L_inst + λ_smooth L_smooth，λ_conf=1、λ_inst=10、λ_smooth=1 [p. 5, 式 (6)]。L_conf 为逐像素 L2 损失，实例像素向二维高斯 u_k(c_im,c_in) 回归，背景向 0 回归 [式 (7)–(8)]。L_inst 为高斯上的交叉熵 [式 (11)]。L_smooth 惩罚预测边界与实例平均边界的偏差 [式 (12)]。中心与边界由式 (9)–(10) 定义。对框标注样本，框内 d_i > 0.5 的前景像素作为伪标签（自学习）[p. 5]。

**第三步——主模型。** 使用原版 Mask R-CNN 或 CenterMask，以真实像素标签加框生成的伪标签训练 [p. 4]。

## 3. 贡献
作者主张：(i) 兼顾标注成本与精度的混合监督流程；(ii) 抑制背景噪声与实例噪声的语义/实例辅助模型；(iii) CASA、类别/实例约束与自学习以充分利用框标签并避免过拟合 [p. 2]。我的解读：核心新意在于“少量干净子集 + 学习式噪声抑制”的建模，而非新的主网络结构；约束模块本质是一致性先验，自学习类似迭代标签精炼。

## 4. 实验与结果
**数据集。** PASCAL VOC 2012 及增强集（10,582 张训练图，20 类），指标 mAP@0.5/0.7/0.75 [p. 7]；Cityscapes（训练 2,975、验证 500、测试 1,525；8 个 thing 类），指标 COCO 风格 mask AP 与 AP50 [p. 7]。

**实现细节。** 语义辅助：Xception-65、ADAM、多项式衰减 (1−iter/maxiter)^0.9、学习率 7e-4、批大小 8、裁剪 512×512（VOC）/640×640（Cityscapes）、交叉熵 + Lovász 损失、60k 迭代、4×GTX 1080 Ti [p. 9]。实例辅助：相同主干/优化器/衰减，学习率 1e-4（VOC）/5e-4→5e-5（Cityscapes），VOC 上 448×448 裁剪训练 60k 迭代批 8；Cityscapes 先在 448×448 上预训练 40k，再在 864×864 上批 2 微调 20k 并冻结 BN；Lovász-hinge 损失；2 块 GPU [p. 9]。主模型：Mask R-CNN ResNet-101（VOC）/ResNet-50（Cityscapes）；CenterMask ResNeXt-152；批 8、学习率 1e-2、权重衰减 1e-4、动量 0.9、24k 迭代、ADAM；CenterMask 在 16k（VOC）/18k（Cityscapes）降至 1e-3，再用像素标签微调 2k；8 块 GPU [p. 10]。

**伪标签质量（表 2）。** 1%（105 张）与 10%（1058 张）像素标签下，mAP@0.5/@0.75 分别为 64.2/39.1 与 70.2/49.3，对比 GrabCut 38.5/13.9、MCG 28.3/5.9 [p. 5]。

**消融（10% 像素标签）。** 语义辅助 mIoU：基线 76.6 → +CASA 86.5 → +类别约束 89.1 → +自学习 90.2（表 5）[p. 9]。伪标签 mAP@0.5/@0.75：21.6/1.8 → +CASA 47.6/28.4 → +语义结果 63.8/38.4 → +实例约束 65.6/43.3 → +自学习 70.1/47.8 → +类别约束 70.2/49.3（表 6）[p. 9]。1% 标签下自学习将 mAP@0.5 从 38.2 提至 64.2、mAP@0.75 从 11.8 提至 39.1；10% 标签下为 70.1→70.2、47.8→49.3（表 7）[p. 10]。

**VOC 对比（表 3，正文见 p. 12）。** Mask R-CNN + 1% 像素标签时，比半监督 Budget-aware（13.8% 像素标签）高 15.0 mAP@0.5；在相近标注成本下（本文 16.7% vs 15.1–15.9%），mAP@0.75 比弱监督 SDI/BBTP/LACI 高约 18.9/13.6/4.0。10% 标签时与全监督 FCIS/Mask R-CNN/CenterMask 相当，mAP@0.7 比 SDS/MNC 高 22.7/6.5。50% 标签时 Mask R-CNN 与 CenterMask 的 mAP@0.75 与全监督持平，节省 42.1% 标注成本 [p. 12]。

**Cityscapes（表 4）。** Mask R-CNN + 1% 标签：AP 19.4，对比弱监督 WSSPS 17.0（WSSPS 用 ResNet-101，本文 ResNet-50；成本 9.2% vs 10.1%）。10% 标签时 AP 28.5，与全监督 SGN（29.2）、Mask R-CNN（31.5）、CenterMask（34.7）相当。CenterMask 变体 1% 标签 AP 18.7；10% 为 30.5；50% 为 34.0，全监督 34.7 [p. 9]。

**语义分割扩展（表 8）。** DeepLabv3+ 用 10% 像素标签达 83.28% mIoU，全监督为 81.21%；13.8% 标签下 83.41%，同等成本下 Ibrahim 等为 82.33% [p. 12]。

## 5. 评估
有支持：消融一致表明各模块提升伪标签质量，1% 标签下自学习作用最大；对比多在相近标注成本下进行。局限/缺失证据：未设计对噪声鲁棒的主模型（列为未来工作）[p. 14]；表 3 在提供文本中不可读，VOC 数字仅来自正文叙述；未报告方差/随机种子；优于含噪 SBD 真值（图 9）仅为定性；Cityscapes 上相对全监督仍有差距（如 10% 时 30.5 vs 34.7 AP）。正文与表格存在个别表述不一致（如 Cityscapes 中 WSSPS 对比措辞）。

## 6. 复现
已报告：数据集/划分、标签预算（1/3/5/10/20/50%）、主干、优化器、学习率、调度、裁剪尺寸、批大小、迭代数、GPU 数、损失权重（1/10/1）、置信度阈值 0.5、偏移范围 [−1,1] 映射到 [−512,512]/[−1024,1024] 像素 [p. 9]。未报告：辅助模型的具体数据增强、随机种子、代码发布、表 1 统计之外“标注成本”百分比的确切定义，以及表 3 的完整数值（不可读）。

notes_en.full_md:
## 1. Problem and motivation
Fully supervised instance segmentation depends on large pixel-wise labeled datasets, which are expensive: the authors cite ~79 s to draw a segmentation versus ~7 s for a bounding box, about 11.3× more costly [p. 1]. Weakly supervised methods using image-level or box labels reduce cost but lose accuracy; the authors attribute this to two noise types in box labels (Fig. 1): **background noise** (background pixels inside a box labeled foreground) and **instance noise** (pixels of overlapping boxes assigned to the wrong instance) [pp. 1–3]. They formalize these as probabilities q0 (background mislabeled as foreground) and q1 (foreground pixels assigned to an incorrect instance) in Eq. (1) [p. 3]. Prior box-supervised works rely on hand-crafted heuristics (GrabCut, MCG) or multiple-instance learning and cannot use pixel-wise labels to refine pseudo labels [p. 3]. The goal is to keep labeling cost low while retaining accuracy by combining a small clean pixel-wise subset with box labels.

## 2. Method
The pipeline is a three-step cascade (Fig. 2) used only at training time; the primary model runs independently afterward [p. 2].

**Step 1 – semantic ancillary model.** Based on DeepLabv3+ (Xception-65 backbone), it predicts semantic segmentation Y′ = f_θ(X, h_CASA(B)) to separate foreground from background inside boxes, suppressing background noise [p. 4, Eq. (2)].

**Step 2 – instance ancillary model.** Also DeepLabv3+-based, but the decoder is split into two branches (confidence and instance) with 4× upsampling (two deconvolution layers with a residual block between them) [p. 4]. It uses the spatial-embedding loss of Neven et al. The instance branch predicts pixel offset maps (o_im, o_in) giving predicted centers c_im = o_im + e_im, c_in = o_in + e_in [Eq. (3)], plus margin maps (r_im, r_in) adapted to instance size/shape. The confidence branch predicts a per-pixel confidence d_i; d_i ≤ 0.5 is treated as background. At inference, the highest-confidence foreground pixel in each category-specific box gives the estimated center and margins; pixels are clustered to instance S_k if the Gaussian distance in Eq. (4) exceeds 0.5 [p. 4]. Output is pseudo instance labels Y″ = g_φ(X, h_CASA(B, Y′)) [Eq. (5)].

**Category-aware spatial attention (CASA).** Two CASA blocks at 4× and 16× downsampling scales fuse box-label and intermediate segmentation information into backbone features [p. 5]. Each block has a category branch (global max/average pooling + MLP → channel attention F_c ∈ R^{N×1×1}) and a shape branch (1×1 conv + sigmoid → spatial attention F_s ∈ R^{N×H×W}), with an extra 3×3 conv to emphasize boundaries; fusion is element-wise multiplication [p. 5].

**Category and instance constraint modules.** The category constraint restricts each pixel inside a non-overlapping box to background or that box's category, removing false positives outside boxes [p. 5]. The instance constraint filters the confidence map outside each box before clustering, preventing nearby objects from merging [p. 5].

**Self-learning.** Pseudo labels from box-labeled images are used to optimize the ancillary models themselves, ignoring losses from uncertain-category pixels (max confidence < 0.5) and overlapping-box regions, to avoid overfitting with few pixel-wise labels [p. 5].

**Losses.** Total loss L_total = λ_conf L_conf + λ_inst L_inst + λ_smooth L_smooth with λ_conf=1, λ_inst=10, λ_smooth=1 [p. 5, Eq. (6)]. L_conf is a pixel-wise L2 loss toward a 2D Gaussian u_k(c_im,c_in) for instance pixels and 0 for background [Eq. (7)–(8)]. L_inst is cross-entropy on the Gaussian [Eq. (11)]. L_smooth penalizes deviation of predicted margins from instance-mean margins [Eq. (12)]. Centers and margins are defined by Eqs. (9)–(10). For box-labeled samples, foreground pixels with d_i > 0.5 inside a box serve as pseudo labels (self-learning) [p. 5].

**Step 3 – primary model.** Vanilla Mask R-CNN or CenterMask trained on ground-truth pixel labels plus pseudo labels from boxes [p. 4].

## 3. Contribution
Authors claim: (i) a hybrid pipeline balancing labeling cost and accuracy; (ii) semantic and instance ancillary models that suppress background and instance noise; (iii) CASA, category/instance constraints, and self-learning to exploit box labels and avoid overfitting [p. 2]. My interpretation: the core novelty is the learned noise-suppression formulation with a small clean subset, rather than new primary architectures; the constraint modules are largely consistency priors, and the self-learning resembles iterative label refinement.

## 4. Experiments and results
**Datasets.** PASCAL VOC 2012 + augmented set (10,582 training images, 20 classes) with mAP@0.5/0.7/0.75 [p. 7]; Cityscapes (2,975 train, 500 val, 1,525 test; 8 thing classes) with COCO-style mask AP and AP50 [p. 7].

**Implementation.** Semantic ancillary: Xception-65, ADAM, polynomial decay (1−iter/maxiter)^0.9, lr 7e-4, batch 8, crops 512×512 (VOC) / 640×640 (Cityscapes), cross-entropy + Lovász loss, 60k iters, 4×GTX 1080 Ti [p. 9]. Instance ancillary: same backbone/optimizer/decay, lr 1e-4 (VOC) / 5e-4→5e-5 (Cityscapes), 448×448 crops 60k iters batch 8 (VOC); Cityscapes pre-train 40k on 448×448 then 20k on 864×864 batch 2 with frozen BN; Lovász-hinge loss; 2 GPUs [p. 9]. Primary: Mask R-CNN ResNet-101 (VOC) / ResNet-50 (Cityscapes); CenterMask ResNeXt-152; batch 8, lr 1e-2, weight decay 1e-4, momentum 0.9, 24k iters, ADAM; CenterMask lr drops to 1e-3 at 16k (VOC)/18k (Cityscapes), then 2k fine-tune on pixel labels; 8 GPUs [p. 10].

**Pseudo-label quality (Table 2).** With 1% (105) and 10% (1058) pixel labels, mAP@0.5/@0.75 = 64.2/39.1 and 70.2/49.3, versus GrabCut 38.5/13.9 and MCG 28.3/5.9 [p. 5].

**Ablations (10% pixel labels).** Semantic ancillary mIoU: baseline 76.6 → +CASA 86.5 → +category constraint 89.1 → +self-learning 90.2 (Table 5) [p. 9]. Pseudo-label mAP@0.5/@0.75: 21.6/1.8 → +CASA 47.6/28.4 → +semantic result 63.8/38.4 → +instance constraint 65.6/43.3 → +self-learning 70.1/47.8 → +category constraint 70.2/49.3 (Table 6) [p. 9]. Self-learning with 1% labels raises mAP@0.5 from 38.2 to 64.2 and mAP@0.75 from 11.8 to 39.1; with 10% labels, 70.1→70.2 and 47.8→49.3 (Table 7) [p. 10].

**VOC comparisons (Table 3, referenced p. 12).** With Mask R-CNN and 1% pixel labels, the method beats semi-supervised Budget-aware (13.8% pixel labels) by 15.0 mAP@0.5, and weakly supervised SDI/BBTP/LACI by ~18.9/13.6/4.0 mAP@0.75 at similar labeling cost (ours 16.7% vs 15.1–15.9%). With 10% labels it is comparable to fully supervised FCIS/Mask R-CNN/CenterMask and beats SDS/MNC by 22.7/6.5 mAP@0.7. With 50% labels, Mask R-CNN and CenterMask match full-supervision mAP@0.75, saving 42.1% labeling cost [p. 12].

**Cityscapes (Table 4).** Mask R-CNN with 1% labels: AP 19.4 vs weakly supervised WSSPS 17.0 (WSSPS uses ResNet-101 vs our ResNet-50; cost 9.2% vs 10.1%). With 10% labels, AP 28.5 comparable to fully supervised SGN (29.2), Mask R-CNN (31.5), CenterMask (34.7). CenterMask variant with 1% labels: AP 18.7; 10%: 30.5; 50%: 34.0 vs full 34.7 [p. 9].

**Semantic extension (Table 8).** DeepLabv3+ with 10% pixel labels reaches 83.28% mIoU vs fully supervised 81.21%, and 13.8% labels gives 83.41% vs Ibrahim et al. 82.33% at equal cost [p. 12].

## 5. Assessment
Supported: ablations consistently show each module improves pseudo-label quality, and self-learning matters most at 1% labels. Comparisons are mostly at similar labeling cost. Limitations/missing evidence: the paper does not design a noise-robust primary model (stated as future work) [p. 14]; Table 3 is not readable in the supplied text, so VOC numbers are taken from prose only; no variance/seed reporting; the claim of beating noisy SBD ground truth (Fig. 9) is qualitative; Cityscapes gains over full supervision remain notable (e.g., 30.5 vs 34.7 AP at 10%). Some prose/table inconsistencies exist (e.g., Cityscapes WSSPS comparison wording).

## 6. Reproduction
Reported: datasets/splits, label budgets (1/3/5/10/20/50%), backbones, optimizers, learning rates, schedules, crop sizes, batch sizes, iteration counts, GPU counts, loss weights (1/10/1), confidence threshold 0.5, offset range [−1,1] mapping to [−512,512]/[−1024,1024] pixels [p. 9]. Unreported: exact data augmentation for ancillary models, random seeds, code release, precise definition of "labeling cost" percentages beyond Table 1 statistics, and full Table 3 values (unreadable).

summary: Current surgical scene graph generation methods depend on dense multi-modal supervision and specialized hardware (synchronized RGB-D sensors, calibration rigs), making dataset construction expensive and restricting all existing benchmarks to simulated environments. We propose SAGE-OR, a feature-centric framework that replaces the traditional detect-then-reason paradigm with a decoupled representation-reasoning paradigm in which localization is derived from frozen foundation models, encoded implicitly in pre-computed features, and used without any localization supervision, while a lightweight graph transformer performs relational reasoning over cached features. We employ a semi-supervised formulation with general-purpose segmentation prompts to eliminate localization supervision while enabling unsupervised context augmentation through additional prompt-driven entities, such as hands, which are absent from annotations. General-purpose prompts are used to induce near-perfect recall, while precision is delegated to downstream attention-based reasoning, enabling simple adaptation to new entities via prompt-level modification. This design enables a lightweight 15M-parameter graph transformer that trains in 1.4 hours and runs relational inference at $\sim$1ms per frame with peak memory under 2GB, suitable for edge hardware used in the operating room; feature extraction runs offline as a separate caching stage (4.27s per frame). On the 4D-OR benchmark, the core model achieves 76% F1, matching the fully supervised 4D-OR baseline while eliminating all localization annotations, and unsupervised hand augmentation raises this to 86%, within 4 points of state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods requiring dense multi-modal supervision, providing a practical pathway for adaptation to new surgical settings without annotation other than relationship and class labels.

notes_zh.digest_en: SAGE-OR replaces supervised detection in operating-room scene graph generation with a frozen three-stage cache (Pi3 multi-view geometry, SAM3 open-vocabulary segmentation, DINOv3 features) plus a 15M-parameter graph transformer trained only with relationship and class labels via Hungarian matching. On 4D-OR it reports 76% F1 without localization supervision, matching the fully supervised 4D-OR baseline, and 86% F1 after adding unannotated hand prompts as unsupervised context nodes; irrelevant control prompts give no gain. The trainable model trains in 1.4 h and runs relational inference at ~1 ms/frame on cached features, but cache generation costs 4.27 s/frame offline and evaluation is limited to one simulated benchmark.
notes_zh.digest_zh: SAGE-OR 用冻结的三阶段缓存（Pi3 多视角几何、SAM3 开放词表分割、DINOv3 特征）替代手术室场景图生成中的监督式检测，再用仅 15M 参数的图 Transformer 通过匈牙利匹配、只依赖关系与类别标签训练。在 4D-OR 上，无任何定位监督时报告 76% F1，与全监督 4D-OR 基线持平；把未标注的“手”作为无监督上下文节点加入提示词后升至 86% F1，而无关控制提示词没有增益。可训练模型训练 1.4 小时，缓存特征上的关系推理约 1 ms/帧；但缓存生成离线需 4.27 s/帧，且仅在单一模拟基准上评估。
notes_zh.full_md:
## 1. 问题与动机

手术室（OR）场景图生成（SGG）可用于工作流识别与安全监控，但作者认为其落地受两大问题阻碍：密集多模态监督与适应性差 [p. 1]。现有方法（LABRAD-OR、S2Former-OR、TriTemp-OR）需要逐帧边界框、人体姿态、分割掩码、场景/物体点云与度量深度，外加关系与类别标注 [p. 1]。所有外部 OR 数据集均为模拟场景，所需的同步 RGB-D 设备与标定在真实手术室中难以被接受；MM-OR 反而增加模态而非降低要求 [p. 2]。要适应新术式（如机器人辅助与手动膝关节置换），现有方法需重新完整标注数据集，且无法在不重训检测的情况下加入新实体类型 [p. 2]。作者的核心假设是：若用冻结的基础模型预计算足够丰富的实例特征，显式定位监督就不再必要——对应关系可由二分匹配学习，几何信息保留在特征空间，身份由自监督表征捕获 [p. 2]。

## 2. 方法

**阶段一：缓存生成（全部冻结、离线）。** 对每帧 N 个视角，Pi3 输出稠密 H×W×3 点图、逐像素置信度与相对相机位姿；点被变换到共享世界坐标系，从而无需深度传感器、标定或 SfM 即可获得 3D 结构 [p. 4]。SAM3 使用通用类别提示（如 person、medical table、tool）而非细粒度手术类别；作者刻意以召回率为先，因为假阳性会成为未匹配节点，而假阴性无法在下游恢复 [p. 5]。掩码被提升到 3D，并通过类别约束的 3D IoU 聚类跨视角融合；报告设置为置信度阈值 0.1、3D IoU 阈值 0.15、最少 10 个点、体素大小为场景包围盒对角线的 2% 以处理 Pi3 的尺度歧义 [p. 5; p. 17-20]。超参数在训练集上对置信度 [0,0.5]、密度 [5,30]、IoU [0.05,0.3] 做网格搜索，以最大化实例召回并保持图稳定 [p. 5]。DINOv3 特征采用混合策略：大实体用 392×518 低分辨率输入（每实例 50-200 个 patch），工具/手用 1536×2048 高分辨率裁剪、20% 框填充并缩放至 518×518（约 300 个 patch，密度约 100 倍），跨视角均值池化 [p. 5; p. 21-22]。缓存存储视觉特征 v_i、13 维几何特征 g_i 与 5 维类别提示 c_i，半精度下每实例约 2 KB [p. 5; p. 20]。

**阶段二：图 Transformer。** 每个节点拼接视觉特征、3D 质心与类别提示，线性投影后加入世界质心的 3D 正弦位置编码，再通过所有节点间的注意力进行上下文建模 [p. 5; p. 23]。注意力 logits 加入由质心两两欧氏距离 d_ij 经学习得到的偏置 φ(d_ij)，使邻近实体注意力更强 [p. 5; 式 S15, p. 23]。2 层 MLP 输出 12 类 logits；这些类别先验以停止梯度方式传给边头，使边梯度不影响节点分类 [p. 5-6]。对每个有序节点对，边特征融合节点嵌入及其差向量、停止梯度的类别先验、类别提示与 11 维成对几何描述子 g_ij = [d_ij, r̂_ij, Δz_ij, log(s_j/s_i+1), log(V_j/V_i+1), IoU_3D(i,j), d_ij/s̄_ij]，各分量分别归一化 [p. 6, 式 1]。所有成对特征送入 2 层边 Transformer（4 头，维度 512），使边之间相互注意以实现全局一致性，再由线性头输出 15 类关系 logits [p. 6; p. 24]。

**阶段三：半监督损失。** 由于没有定位标签，对应关系由匈牙利匹配学习：若 SAM3 类别与 GT 类别兼容，代价 C_ij = 1−P(y_j|x_i)，否则为 ∞（例如 person 实例可匹配任何人类角色，但绝不匹配器械）[p. 7, 式 2; 兼容集合 V(·) 见式 S22-S26, p. 24]。总目标为 L = λ_node L_node + λ_edge L_edge + λ_proxy L_proxy，λ_node=1.0、λ_edge=2.0、λ_proxy=1.0 [p. 7, 式 3]。L_node 与 L_edge 为匹配对上的交叉熵；边损失按逆类别频率加权（none 类权重 0.0001）[p. 7; 式 S32-S33, p. 24]。L_proxy 为帧级 14 类（不含 none）多标签 BCE，带 pos_weight 平衡，沿用 LABRAD-OR 以稳定稀有关系 [p. 7, 式 4; p. 25]。未匹配预测不获监督，但仍作为无标签上下文参与注意力；未匹配 GT 视为漏检 [p. 7]。这正是无监督上下文增强的机制来源。

## 3. 贡献

作者主张的贡献 [p. 2-3]：(1) 基于匈牙利匹配的半监督训练，无需框、姿态、掩码、深度或点云，并由此实现无监督上下文增强（未标注的手带来 +10 F1）；(2) 解耦的特征缓存框架，仅用 RGB，无需深度传感器、标定，且因 Pi3 支持任意/单目配置而不限制视角数；(3) 首次对手术 SGG 的现代视觉编码器做系统比较；(4) 解耦推理高效（缓存特征上约 1 ms/帧）；(5) 声称是首个仅需 RGB 与稀疏场景图标注、同时保留空间定位的可适应 OR-SGG 框架。我的解读：真正有特色的是“召回优先的开放词表提示 + 基于匹配的隐式定位 + 注意力利用未标注节点”这一组合；各组件（Pi3、SAM3、DINOv3、匈牙利匹配、DETR 式集合预测）均为已有技术。文中的“首次”主张是断言，未以穷尽文献检索证明。

## 4. 实验与结果

**设置。** 4D-OR：10 段膝关节置换录像、6,734 帧、6 个同步 RGB-D 视角、分辨率 1536×2048；12 个实体类、15 个关系类（14 种关系 + none）；按先前工作 6 段训练 / 2 段验证 / 2 段测试；在留出测试集上对 15 个关系类做宏平均 P/R/F1 [p. 7]。D_g=13、D_p=11、N_c=5 [p. 7]。图 Transformer：隐藏维 384、4 层、6 头、dropout 0.3；边 Transformer 2 层、4 头、隐藏维 512；最多 200 epoch（消融 100），batch 4，AdamW，学习率 3×10⁻⁵，权重衰减 10⁻⁴，余弦调度含 10 个 warmup epoch；子图采样保留率 U[0.5,0.9]；单张 RTX Ada 6000（48 GB），峰值内存 <2 GB；约 15M 可训练参数，训练约 1.4 小时 [p. 7-8]。

**SOTA 对比（表 1, p. 8）。** SAGE-OR 核心：平均 F1 76%，15M 参数，0.001 s/场景（仅图推理），监督为“关系 + 类别”。SAGE-OR 完整版（+hands）：86% F1。基线：4D-OR 75% F1（84.8M，1.28 s）、LABRAD-OR 88%（85.8M，1.46 s，时序）、S2Former-OR 89%（60.6M，0.98 s）、TriTemp-OR 90%（67.1M，时序）、Pix2SG 平均 F1 91% 但非空间定位且为自回归 [p. 8]。作者将 4 点差距分解为约 3 点来自监督减少（相对 S2Former-OR），其余来自缺少时序建模 [p. 8]。他们指出 Assisting 与 Touching 对所有方法都难（全监督 4D-OR 与 S2Former-OR 在 Touching 上低于 SAGE-OR 的 62%）[p. 8]。

**节点分类（表 3, p. 10）。** 用类别 logits 与 SAM3 约束做匈牙利匹配后，总节点准确率 0.99；Patient F1 0.99、Anesthesia Equipment 1.00、Human_0 0.99、Human_1 1.00、Human_2 0.98、Human_3 0.76（支持数 101）、Human_4 0.00（支持数 2）、Human_5 0.00（支持数 0）、Instrument/Instrument Table/Operating Table/Secondary Table 均为 1.00 [p. 10]。作者据此认为身份消歧已解决，瓶颈在关系推理 [p. 8]。

**无监督手部增强（表 2, p. 9）。** 加入“hand”提示（数据集中无手部标注）使平均 F1 从 76 升至 86，召回从 75 升至 86；逐类 ΔF1：Cementing +25、Suturing +25、Sawing +25、Cutting +17、Hammering +12、Cleaning +8、Touching +6，其余 +0 至 +3 [p. 9]。流程只需增加一个提示词、重新生成缓存并在不改架构/损失的情况下重训 [p. 9]。控制实验（表 4, p. 10；表 S4, p. 25）：knee（5,916 次检测）、door（29,905）、shoe（32,264）相对仅手部基线 82% F1 的 ΔF1 均为 0 [p. 10; p. 25]。注意控制实验基线为 82%，而非主表 86%，控制实验内部自洽但与表 2 数值不一致。作者称手是唯一可行的未标注实体，且这属于基准内适应，而非适应新术式 [p. 9]。

**编码器分析（表 6, p. 10）。** DINOv3 ViT-L/16：F1 82%（P 78、R 88、1784 MB）；ViT-B/16 81；ViT-S/16 77；ViT-7B/16 67（3056 MB，归因于过拟合）；CLIP ViT-L/14 75；EfficientNet-B5-NS 74；ResNet-50 66 [p. 10]。作者结论是自监督特征更丰富，最佳编码器并非最大者 [p. 10]。

**特征/增强消融（表 7-9, p. 10-11）。** 基础（节点+几何）F1 82%；加入类别提示、物体类型、类别先验、成对几何或全部融合为 80-82%；“全部特征”82%；35M 参数模型 82%（无增益）；去掉 proxy 损失 80%（−2）[p. 10]。视觉特征消融：全部特征 82%；去掉边视觉特征仍 82%，节省 200 MB、2M 参数并提升 200 FPS；去掉节点视觉特征降至 53%；仅几何 54% [p. 11]。增强消融：无 80%，子图采样 82%（召回 83→87），+节点 dropout 80%，+特征 dropout 78% [p. 11]。缓存开销（表 5, p. 10）：SAM3 2.58 s/帧（4.92 h，5097 MB，61%）、Pi3 0.56 s（1.05 h，6464 MB，13%）、DINOv3 1.13 s（2.12 h，1736 MB，26%），合计 4.27 s/帧、8.1 h、峰值 6464 MB [p. 10]。

## 5. 评估

有证据支持的结论：核心模型在无定位标注下达到 76% F1，在所述协议下与全监督 4D-OR 基线 75% 持平 [p. 8]；手部增强的增益有控制实验佐证——节点数相当的无关提示词没有带来变化 [p. 10; p. 25]；主要实体的节点分类接近完美 [p. 10]；效率主张（15M 参数、1.4 小时、图推理约 1 ms/帧）附有硬件说明 [p. 7-8]。局限与缺失证据：仅在 4D-OR 这一单一模拟膝关节置换基准上评估，作者亦承认 [p. 11]；86% 仍落后 S2Former-OR（89%）与 TriTemp-OR（90%）[p. 8]；所展示的“适应”只是基准内加入一个未标注实体，作者明确将新术式适应留作未来工作 [p. 9]；缓存生成离线需 4.27 s/帧、峰值 6.4 GB，未展示实时部署 [p. 10]；控制实验基线（82%）与主增强结果（86%）不同，文中未作解释；“首次”主张及“手是唯一可行未标注实体”依赖作者审阅而非正式检索 [p. 3; p. 9]；未报告统计方差或多随机种子；与 Pix2SG（91%）的对比并非同口径，因其非空间定位 [p. 8]。

## 6. 复现

已报告步骤：(1) 获取 4D-OR 并使用 6/2/2 分段划分 [p. 7]；(2) 对每帧 6 视角运行 Pi3 得到点图、置信度与位姿 [p. 4]；(3) 用 person、medical table、anesthesia equipment、tool in hand（可选 hand）提示运行 SAM3，大实体用 392×518 低分辨率、工具/手用 1536×2048，置信度 0.3（工具 0.01）[p. 15, 表 S1]；(4) 以置信度 0.1、3D IoU 0.15、最少 10 点、体素为场景对角线 2%、类别组 {person}、{table, anesthesia}、{tool, hand} 融合掩码 [p. 5; p. 18-20]；(5) 按混合策略提取 DINOv3 特征并跨视角均值池化 [p. 21-22]；(6) 按所述架构与优化器设置、匈牙利匹配与损失权重训练图 Transformer [p. 7-8; p. 23-25]。未报告或不明确：Pi3/SAM3/DINOv3 的具体检查点版本与推理批设置；精确训练迭代数/早停规则；随机种子与方差；子图采样除保留率范围外的具体实现；82% 控制基线如何对应 86% 主结果；部分基线的完整逐类数字在所提供的表格渲染中仅部分可辨 [p. 8]。

notes_en.digest_en: SAGE-OR replaces supervised detection in operating-room scene graph generation with a frozen three-stage cache (Pi3 multi-view geometry, SAM3 open-vocabulary segmentation, DINOv3 features) plus a 15M-parameter graph transformer trained only with relationship and class labels via Hungarian matching. On 4D-OR it reports 76% F1 without localization supervision, matching the fully supervised 4D-OR baseline, and 86% F1 after adding unannotated hand prompts as unsupervised context nodes; irrelevant control prompts give no gain. The trainable model trains in 1.4 h and runs relational inference at ~1 ms/frame on cached features, but cache generation costs 4.27 s/frame offline and evaluation is limited to one simulated benchmark.
